item.title: 一个基础费管不住两种资源：EIP-7999 多维定价与一维费用机制的模拟对比
item.author: Fei Wu
item.description:
Fei Wu 在 ethresear.ch 发文：提高目标比例或改用 EIP-4844 式更新，都只能让一维机制在执行量、状态增长和拥堵之间换取平衡；在其标定的需求模型下，EIP-7999 在相近或更低拥堵下交付更多执行量，状态增长保持在每年 120 GiB 目标。

中文改写

在以太坊上，把执行 gas 和状态增长放在同一个基础费（base fee）下定价，会出现一个问题：费用只能追着更紧的那项资源走。Fei Wu 在 ethresear.ch 发布的新帖用模拟数据对比了两条路线：继续改进一维费用机制，或者转向 EIP-7999 的多维定价。在标定的需求模型下，EIP-7999 在拥堵相近或更低的情况下交付更多执行量，同时把状态增长保持在每年 120 GiB 的目标上。

这项工作部分完成于作者在以太坊基金会（EF）实习期间，作者感谢导师 misilva73 的讨论和意见。帖子把此前三篇分析（EIP-7999 多维费用市场的均衡分析、动态模拟，以及与 Glamsterdam 之后一维费用市场的对比）合并扩展成一篇论文：《More Meters or More Prices? One- vs. Multi-dimensional Fee Mechanisms on Ethereum》（arXiv 2610.33455）。帖中结果可以用作者公开的代码仓库复现。

起点：最强的一维基准，仍有两项资源达不到目标

上一篇帖子比较了三个一维基准：基线方案（每字节 64 gas 的下限，CPSB = 1530）、下限调整加 EIP-8368、下限调整加 EIP-8372。按当前的资源需求，最强的是下限调整加 EIP-8372，论文称之为“归一化基准”。它的做法是：交易下限价格随每种传播时间分配（propagation allocation）调整；EIP-8372 把 CPSB 和状态 gas 上限按同一个系数缩放，让常规 gas 和状态 gas 在均衡时于同一个基础费下达到各自目标。它保留 EIP-1559 的目标与上限之比 1/2，也保留 EIP-1559 的更新规则。

在区块层面的需求波动下，这个基准每个区块交付 1.519 亿至 1.779 亿执行 gas，但常规 gas 和归一化后的状态 gas 平均都低于目标，状态增长为每年 86.0 至 88.1 GiB，目标是 120 GiB。

论文在此基础上继续推进：先把目标与上限之比提高到最多 4/5，看能否交付更多执行量；发现 EIP-1559 的更新规则成了约束后，换成 EIP-4844 的伪指数（fake exponential）更新；最后与 EIP-7999 比较。全文用近上限区块的占比衡量拥堵，指 gas 用量达到某个硬上限 98% 以上的区块。

提高目标比例：执行量上去了，状态增长和拥堵变差

作者把下限调整加 EIP-8372 的目标与上限之比依次设为 1/2、3/5、2/3、3/4、4/5，每种传播时间分配下的 gas 上限和下限价格不变。每个比例下都重新标定 CPSB，让达到目标时的状态用量仍对应每年 120 GiB，并重新计算 EIP-8372 的缩放系数。

每种分配下，执行量都随比例上升，到 4/5 时达到 1.990 亿至 2.150 亿。代价是状态增长离目标更远，降到每年 56.7 至 68.7 GiB；区块也更拥堵，4/5 时有 13.2% 至 20.6% 的区块接近上限，1/2 时约为 4%。

原因在于 EIP-1559 的更新规则无法把费用降到新的均衡点。 目标越高，出清的费用越低：在 4/5 时，两条分支同时达到目标的基础费只有 2.4 至 7.2 wei。按 EIP-1559，一个低于目标的区块会把基础费降低 ⌊b_t(T_G − G_t) / 8T_G⌋，其中 G_t 是两条分支中用量较大的那一条。除非区块比目标少出至少 8/b_t 的比例，这个降幅都会被取整成零。费用一旦低于 8 wei，任何区块都无法再让它下降，而每个高于目标的区块都会让它至少涨 1 wei。

模拟中费用从未低于 8 wei，平均为 18.3 至 27.2 wei，是均衡值的四到八倍。按均衡计算，4/5 的设计本应交付 2.45 亿至 2.80 亿执行量，模拟中只有 1.990 亿至 2.150 亿。

费用高于均衡会压缩所有资源，状态被压得最多，因为它对价格最敏感。比例提高还降低了每块状态字节上限相对目标的倍数，从 1/2 时的 2 倍降到 4/5 时的 1.25 倍，状态创建的突发会被截断。

换成 EIP-4844 式更新：费用降下来了，拥堵翻倍

为了让费用能降到这么低，作者在 4/5 比例下把 EIP-1559 更新换成 EIP-4844 的持续超额 gas 计数器加伪指数函数，配置和需求路径保持不变：x_{t+1} = max(0, x_t + G_t − T_G)，b_t = fake_exponential(1, x_t, 8T_G)。计数器会保留 EIP-1559 取整丢掉的小额缺口，分母 8T_G 让它的响应速度与 EIP-1559 一致。

下表是两种更新规则在 4/5 比例下的对比，每格箭头前为 EIP-1559，箭头后为 EIP-4844 式：

传播时间 执行量（百万 gas） 状态增长（GiB/年） 近上限区块 平均基础费（wei）
3.0 秒 206.4 → 225.9 64.6 → 96.0 17.7% → 40.8% 22.3 → 6.6
3.5 秒 215.0 → 244.2 56.8 → 94.0 13.2% → 39.1% 18.3 → 3.6
4.0 秒 214.1 → 243.6 56.7 → 94.0 13.4% → 38.8% 18.8 → 3.7
4.5 秒 208.5 → 232.5 61.1 → 95.2 16.0% → 39.6% 21.5 → 5.4
5.0 秒 199.0 → 214.8 68.7 → 95.6 20.6% → 39.9% 27.2 → 10.5

费用接近均衡后，执行量和状态增长都回升了，但还剩两个问题。

拥堵大幅上升。 4/5 比例下上限只是目标的 1.25 倍。费用更低时，需求突发更容易顶到上限，38.8% 至 40.8% 的区块接近上限。

两条分支仍然都低于目标。 常规 gas 平均为目标的 85.8% 至 87.1%，归一化状态 gas 为 78.3% 至 80.0%。费用跟随每个区块中较大的那条分支，这条分支现在平均达到目标的 98.8% 至 100.0%；只要一条分支高于目标，另一条也得付更高的费用。一个费用能让较大的分支保持在目标上，但无法同时照顾两条。 在 1/2 比例下，同样更换更新规则几乎没有影响（执行量变化不到 150 万），因为那里的费用在 48 至 191 wei，取整很少起作用。

与 EIP-7999 对比

作者从上一篇帖子测试过的执行目标和数据目标中，为每种传播时间分配挑出两个 EIP-7999 配置：

  • 保守配置：位于执行与数据前沿之内、均衡执行费高于 1 wei、近上限区块占比不超过历史水平 4.73%（2026 年 2 月至 5 月的 860,505 个主网区块）的配置中，执行量最高的一个。
  • 最大吞吐配置：平均执行量最高的配置。

这里的保守规则比前几篇帖子的“历史锚定”规则更严格，后者允许近上限区块比历史占比多 20%，所以部分选择和数字略有不同。

EIP-7999 在所有配置中都把状态增长保持在每年 120 GiB 的目标上，下限调整加 EIP-8372 的各个变体只有 56.7 至 96.0 GiB。

拥堵相近且都较低时，EIP-7999 多交付 4% 至 34% 的执行量。 保守配置和 1/2 比例下的下限调整加 EIP-8372，近上限区块分别为 1.9% 至 4.4% 和 4.0% 至 4.5%，都接近或低于历史占比。在每种分配下，保守配置多交付 680 万至 5600 万执行 gas。

提高一维方案的目标比例，只能靠增加拥堵来缩小部分执行量差距。 在 4/5 时，下限调整加 EIP-8372 在 3 秒分配下比保守配置多 3280 万，3.5 秒下多 1700 万，更长的分配下则落后；但它有 13.2% 至 20.6% 的区块接近上限，保守配置只有 1.9% 至 4.4%。

拥堵更高时，EIP-7999 仍然交付更多。 最大吞吐配置比 4/5 比例的下限调整加 EIP-8372 多交付 4650 万至 7200 万执行量，近上限区块略多（16.6% 至 32.1%，对比 13.2% 至 20.6%）。与 EIP-4844 式变体相比，它们多交付 1950 万至 5620 万，近上限区块反而更少（16.6% 至 32.1%，对比 38.8% 至 40.8%）。

作者还检查了模拟过的每一次一维运行：上一篇的基线和下限调整加 EIP-8368 基准，五种目标比例下的下限调整加 EIP-8372，以及它的 EIP-4844 式变体，每种都覆盖五种传播时间分配。对每一次运行，同一分配下至少有一个位于执行与数据前沿之内的 EIP-7999 测试配置，执行量更多、状态增长保持在目标上、处于硬上限的区块占比不更高。最小的领先幅度是 680 万，出现在 1/2 比例、3 秒分配下的下限调整加 EIP-8372。

局限

需求标定。 结果依赖于用 2025 年 2 月和 7 月两次 gas 上限提高标定的需求模型，而测试的执行目标远超已观测到的需求。论文用这两次提高前后 21 天、60 天、75 天窗口估计的弹性做了稳健性检验。在每种标定下，基线和下限调整加 EIP-8368 基准里决定共享基础费的仍然是状态；为每种标定重新挑选目标的 EIP-7999，仍比下限调整加 EIP-8372 及其 EIP-4844 式变体交付更多执行量。领先幅度取决于标定，执行需求对价格越不敏感，领先通常越小。

只测了这些变体。 作者只测试了文中描述的一维变体，没有穷尽所有设计。论文还显示，当需求偏离标定值时，一次性标定的 EIP-8372 无法再让两条分支对齐；随需求变化重新标定缩放系数的机制，作者没有测试。

结论

提高目标比例和改进更新规则都能帮到一维机制，但各自带来新的代价。沿用 EIP-1559 更新时，更高的目标比例会压低状态增长、增加拥堵；EIP-4844 式更新恢复了状态增长，代价是让多得多的区块顶到上限。单一基础费跟随瓶颈资源，两种改动都无法让两项资源同时接近目标。作者的结论是：在标定的需求模型下，EIP-7999 交付更多执行量，状态增长保持在目标上，拥堵相近或更低，这支持以太坊在扩容中从“分开计量”转向“分开定价”。 关注 Glamsterdam 之后费用市场设计的读者，可以直接用作者的仓库复现这些模拟，并留意结论对需求标定的依赖。

原文

原文取自 ethresear.ch 帖子的 Markdown 源（/raw/26244）；原帖三张图已移到上方媒体区，正文中以 [Figure N] 标出原位置，图注保留在原位；数学公式保持原帖的 LaTeX 源文本；仅收录主楼。

More Meters or More Prices? One- vs. Multi-dimensional Fee Mechanisms on Ethereum

by Fei Wu. This work was partially conducted during my internship at the EF. I thank my mentor @misilva73 for helpful discussions and comments.

Overview

Previously, we have presented our analyses of the equilibrium and dynamic simulation of EIP-7999's multidimensional fee market, comparison with the post-Glamsterdam one-dimensional fee market. We combine and extend these analyses into a paper: More Meters or More Prices? One- vs. Multi-dimensional Fee Mechanisms on Ethereum.

In the previous post, we studied three one-dimensional benchmarks: the baseline (64-gas-per-byte floor and CPSB = 1530), floor-adjusted + EIP-8368, and floor-adjusted + EIP-8372. The strongest is floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 given the current resource demand, which we call the normalized benchmark in the paper: the transaction floor price is adjusted to each propagation allocation, and EIP-8372 scales CPSB and the state gas limit by a common factor, so that regular gas and state gas reach their targets at the same base fee in equilibrium. It keeps the EIP-1559 target-to-limit ratio of 1/2 and the EIP-1559 update rule. Under block-level demand variation, it delivers 151.9M–177.9M execution gas per block, but regular gas and normalized state gas both stay below their targets on average, giving 86.0–88.1 GiB/year of state growth against the 120 GiB/year target.

In the paper, we push this benchmark further. We first raise its target-to-limit ratio up to 4/5 to see whether it delivers more execution. The EIP-1559 update rule then turns out to be a constraint, because it cannot lower the base fee to the few-wei level that a high target requires. We then replace it with the fake-exponential update of EIP-4844. Finally, we compare these one-dimensional variants with EIP-7999. Throughout, we measure congestion as the share of near-limit blocks, whose gas usage reaches at least 98% of a hard limit. The results presented in this post can be reproduced from this repository.

Main results

  1. A higher target ratio for floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 delivers more execution, but contracts state growth and raises congestion. From 1/2 to 4/5, execution rises from 151.9M–177.9M to 199.0M–215.0M, but state growth falls from 86.0–88.1 to 56.7–68.7 GiB/year, and near-limit blocks rise from about 4% to 13.2%–20.6%. Under the EIP-1559 update, the base fee stays at 18–27 wei on average, far above its 2.4–7.2 wei equilibrium, and state, the most price-responsive resource, contracts the most.

  2. The EIP-1559 update rule prevents the fee from falling. The EIP-4844-style update allows lower fees and supports more execution/state, but brings more congestion. At a 4/5 ratio, execution rises to 214.8M–244.2M and state growth recovers to 94.0–96.0 GiB/year, but 38.8%–40.8% of blocks are near a limit, and regular gas and state gas both still stay below their targets.

  3. EIP-7999 delivers more execution with state growth at its target, at similar or lower congestion. At a similarly low share of near-limit blocks, the conservative EIP-7999 configurations deliver 4%–34% more execution than floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 at 1/2. Against the EIP-4844-style variant, the maximum-throughput configurations deliver 19.5M–56.2M more execution with fewer near-limit blocks.

Raising the target-to-limit ratio

We vary the target-to-limit ratio of floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 over 1/2, 3/5, 2/3, 3/4, and 4/5, keeping the gas limit and floor price of each propagation allocation. At each ratio, we recalibrate CPSB so that state usage at the target still corresponds to 120 GiB/year, and recompute the EIP-8372 scaling factor.

[Figure 1]

One-dimensional floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 benchmark under the EIP-1559 update, across target-to-limit ratios and propagation allocations. (a) Mean execution gas per block. (b) Annualized state growth, with the dashed line marking the 120 GiB/year target. Each point is the mean over the same 32 simulated demand paths.

Execution rises with the ratio at every allocation, reaching 199.0M–215.0M at 4/5. But state growth moves further away from its target, falling to 56.7–68.7 GiB/year, and blocks become more congested: at 4/5, 13.2%–20.6% of blocks are near a limit, against about 4% at 1/2.

The EIP-1559 update cannot lower the fee to its new equilibrium. A higher target clears at a much lower fee: at 4/5, the base fee at which both branches reach their targets is only 2.4–7.2 wei. Under EIP-1559, a block below the target lowers the base fee by

$$ \left\lfloor \frac{b_t,(T_G-G_t)}{8T_G}\right\rfloor, $$

where G_t is the gas usage of the larger branch. This decrease rounds to zero unless the block falls short of the target by at least 8/b_t of it. Once the fee is below 8 wei, no block can lower it, while every block above the target raises it by at least 1 wei. In the simulations, the fee never falls below 8 wei and averages 18.3–27.2 wei, about four to eight times its equilibrium value. In equilibrium, the 4/5 design would deliver 245M–280M of execution; in simulation, it delivers 199.0M–215.0M.

A fee above equilibrium contracts every resource, but state the most, because state is the most price-responsive resource. A higher ratio also lowers the per-block state byte limit relative to the target, from twice the target at 1/2 to 1.25 times at 4/5, which clips bursts of state creation.

Replacing the EIP-1559 update with an EIP-4844-style update

To let the fee reach these low levels, we replace the EIP-1559 update of floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 at a 4/5 ratio with the persistent excess-gas counter and fake exponential of EIP-4844, keeping the configurations and demand paths fixed:

$$ x_{t+1}=\max\left(0,;x_t+G_t-T_G\right), \qquad b_t=\mathtt{fake_exponential}\left(1,;x_t,;8T_G\right). $$

The counter keeps the small shortfalls that EIP-1559 rounds away, and the denominator 8T_G matches the response of EIP-1559. The table compares the two update rules at a 4/5 ratio. Each cell shows the EIP-1559 result followed by the EIP-4844-style result.

Propagation Execution (M) State growth (GiB/year) Near-limit blocks Mean base fee (wei)
3.0s 206.4 → 225.9 64.6 → 96.0 17.7% → 40.8% 22.3 → 6.6
3.5s 215.0 → 244.2 56.8 → 94.0 13.2% → 39.1% 18.3 → 3.6
4.0s 214.1 → 243.6 56.7 → 94.0 13.4% → 38.8% 18.8 → 3.7
4.5s 208.5 → 232.5 61.1 → 95.2 16.0% → 39.6% 21.5 → 5.4
5.0s 199.0 → 214.8 68.7 → 95.6 20.6% → 39.9% 27.2 → 10.5

With the EIP-4844-style update, the fee gets close to its equilibrium, so execution and state growth both recover. Two problems remain.

Congestion rises sharply. At a 4/5 ratio, the limit is only 1.25 times the target. With a lower fee, demand bursts reach the limit far more often, and 38.8%–40.8% of blocks are near a limit.

Both branches still stay below their targets. Regular gas averages 85.8%–87.1% of the target and normalized state gas 78.3%–80.0%. The fee follows the larger of the two branches in each block, which now averages 98.8%–100.0% of the target, so whenever one branch is above target, the other pays the higher fee as well. One fee can keep the larger branch on target, but not both. At a 1/2 ratio, the same change of update rule makes almost no difference (execution changes by less than 1.5M), because the fee there is 48–191 wei and rounding rarely matters.

Comparison with EIP-7999

We compare these one-dimensional variants with the two EIP-7999 selected configurations mentioned in the previous post, chosen from the tested execution and data targets at each propagation allocation:

  • Conservative: the highest-execution configuration inside the execution–data frontier, so that its equilibrium execution fee is above 1 wei, and whose share of near-limit blocks does not exceed the historical 4.73% (860,505 mainnet blocks from February to May 2026).
  • Maximum throughput: the configuration with the highest mean execution.

The conservative rule is stricter than the "historically anchored" rule of the previous posts, which allowed 20% more near-limit blocks than the historical share, so some selections and numbers differ slightly.

[Figure 2]

Mean execution gas per block of the one-dimensional floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 benchmark ("One-dimensional EIP-8372") at target-to-limit ratios of 1/2 and 4/5, and of the two EIP-7999 selections, under the same 32 demand paths. Labels are in millions of gas per block.

[Figure 3]

Share of near-limit blocks, whose gas usage reaches at least 98% of a hard limit, for the same designs and the EIP-4844-style variant of floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 at 4/5. The dashed line marks the historical share of 4.73% on mainnet from February to May 2026.

EIP-7999 keeps state growth at its 120 GiB/year target in every configuration, while the floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 variants deliver 56.7–96.0 GiB/year.

At similarly low congestion, EIP-7999 delivers 4%–34% more execution. The conservative configurations and floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 at 1/2 have 1.9%–4.4% and 4.0%–4.5% of blocks near a limit, both close to or below the historical share. The conservative configurations deliver 6.8M–56.0M more execution at every allocation.

A higher one-dimensional target ratio closes part of the execution gap only by raising congestion. At 4/5, floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 exceeds the conservative configurations by 32.8M at 3 seconds and 17.0M at 3.5 seconds and falls behind at longer allocations, but with 13.2%–20.6% of blocks near a limit, against 1.9%–4.4%.

At higher congestion, EIP-7999 still delivers more. The maximum-throughput configurations deliver 46.5M–72.0M more execution than floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 at 4/5, with somewhat more near-limit blocks (16.6%–32.1% against 13.2%–20.6%). Against the EIP-4844-style variant, they deliver 19.5M–56.2M more execution with fewer near-limit blocks (16.6%–32.1% against 38.8%–40.8%).

More generally, we checked every one-dimensional run we simulated: the baseline and floor-adjusted + EIP-8368 benchmarks of the previous post, floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 at the five target ratios, and its EIP-4844-style variant, each at five propagation allocations. For each run, at least one tested EIP-7999 configuration at the same allocation, inside the execution–data frontier, delivers more execution, keeps state growth at its target, and has no larger share of blocks at a hard limit. The smallest such margin is 6.8M, for floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 at 1/2 and 3 seconds.

Limitations

Demand calibration. The results are conditional on the demand model calibrated from the February and July 2025 gas-limit increases, and the tested execution targets extend well beyond observed demand. In the paper, we test robustness to elasticities estimated from 21-, 60-, and 75-day windows around these increases. Under every calibration, state still sets the shared base fee in the baseline and floor-adjusted + EIP-8368 benchmarks, and EIP-7999, with its targets reselected for each calibration, still delivers more execution than floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 and its EIP-4844-style variant. The size of the gain depends on the calibration and is generally smaller when execution demand is less price-responsive.

Tested variants only. We tested the one-dimensional variants described here, not every possible design. The paper also shows that a one-time EIP-8372 calibration no longer aligns the two branches when demand differs from the calibration, and we did not test a mechanism that recalibrates the scaling factor as demand changes.

Conclusion

Raising the target ratio and improving the update rule both help the one-dimensional mechanism, but each brings a new cost. Under the EIP-1559 update, a higher target ratio cuts state growth and raises congestion. The EIP-4844-style update recovers state growth only by letting far more blocks reach the limit. Because the one single base fee follows the bottleneck resource, neither change keeps both near their targets. Under the calibrated demand model, EIP-7999 delivers more execution with state growth at its target, at similar or lower congestion, which supports moving from separate metering to separate pricing as Ethereum scales.

原文链接：https://ethresear.ch/t/more-meters-or-more-prices-one-vs-multi-dimensional-fee-mechanisms-on-ethereum/26244

相关链接：https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33455
item.content:encoded:
Fei Wu 在 ethresear.ch 发文：提高目标比例或改用 EIP-4844 式更新，都只能让一维机制在执行量、状态增长和拥堵之间换取平衡；在其标定的需求模型下，EIP-7999 在相近或更低拥堵下交付更多执行量，状态增长保持在每年 120 GiB 目标。

中文改写

在以太坊上，把执行 gas 和状态增长放在同一个基础费（base fee）下定价，会出现一个问题：费用只能追着更紧的那项资源走。Fei Wu 在 ethresear.ch 发布的新帖用模拟数据对比了两条路线：继续改进一维费用机制，或者转向 EIP-7999 的多维定价。在标定的需求模型下，EIP-7999 在拥堵相近或更低的情况下交付更多执行量，同时把状态增长保持在每年 120 GiB 的目标上。

这项工作部分完成于作者在以太坊基金会（EF）实习期间，作者感谢导师 misilva73 的讨论和意见。帖子把此前三篇分析（EIP-7999 多维费用市场的均衡分析、动态模拟，以及与 Glamsterdam 之后一维费用市场的对比）合并扩展成一篇论文：《More Meters or More Prices? One- vs. Multi-dimensional Fee Mechanisms on Ethereum》（arXiv 2610.33455）。帖中结果可以用作者公开的代码仓库复现。

起点：最强的一维基准，仍有两项资源达不到目标

上一篇帖子比较了三个一维基准：基线方案（每字节 64 gas 的下限，CPSB = 1530）、下限调整加 EIP-8368、下限调整加 EIP-8372。按当前的资源需求，最强的是下限调整加 EIP-8372，论文称之为“归一化基准”。它的做法是：交易下限价格随每种传播时间分配（propagation allocation）调整；EIP-8372 把 CPSB 和状态 gas 上限按同一个系数缩放，让常规 gas 和状态 gas 在均衡时于同一个基础费下达到各自目标。它保留 EIP-1559 的目标与上限之比 1/2，也保留 EIP-1559 的更新规则。

在区块层面的需求波动下，这个基准每个区块交付 1.519 亿至 1.779 亿执行 gas，但常规 gas 和归一化后的状态 gas 平均都低于目标，状态增长为每年 86.0 至 88.1 GiB，目标是 120 GiB。

论文在此基础上继续推进：先把目标与上限之比提高到最多 4/5，看能否交付更多执行量；发现 EIP-1559 的更新规则成了约束后，换成 EIP-4844 的伪指数（fake exponential）更新；最后与 EIP-7999 比较。全文用近上限区块的占比衡量拥堵，指 gas 用量达到某个硬上限 98% 以上的区块。

提高目标比例：执行量上去了，状态增长和拥堵变差

作者把下限调整加 EIP-8372 的目标与上限之比依次设为 1/2、3/5、2/3、3/4、4/5，每种传播时间分配下的 gas 上限和下限价格不变。每个比例下都重新标定 CPSB，让达到目标时的状态用量仍对应每年 120 GiB，并重新计算 EIP-8372 的缩放系数。

每种分配下，执行量都随比例上升，到 4/5 时达到 1.990 亿至 2.150 亿。代价是状态增长离目标更远，降到每年 56.7 至 68.7 GiB；区块也更拥堵，4/5 时有 13.2% 至 20.6% 的区块接近上限，1/2 时约为 4%。

原因在于 EIP-1559 的更新规则无法把费用降到新的均衡点。 目标越高，出清的费用越低：在 4/5 时，两条分支同时达到目标的基础费只有 2.4 至 7.2 wei。按 EIP-1559，一个低于目标的区块会把基础费降低 ⌊b_t(T_G − G_t) / 8T_G⌋，其中 G_t 是两条分支中用量较大的那一条。除非区块比目标少出至少 8/b_t 的比例，这个降幅都会被取整成零。费用一旦低于 8 wei，任何区块都无法再让它下降，而每个高于目标的区块都会让它至少涨 1 wei。

模拟中费用从未低于 8 wei，平均为 18.3 至 27.2 wei，是均衡值的四到八倍。按均衡计算，4/5 的设计本应交付 2.45 亿至 2.80 亿执行量，模拟中只有 1.990 亿至 2.150 亿。

费用高于均衡会压缩所有资源，状态被压得最多，因为它对价格最敏感。比例提高还降低了每块状态字节上限相对目标的倍数，从 1/2 时的 2 倍降到 4/5 时的 1.25 倍，状态创建的突发会被截断。

换成 EIP-4844 式更新：费用降下来了，拥堵翻倍

为了让费用能降到这么低，作者在 4/5 比例下把 EIP-1559 更新换成 EIP-4844 的持续超额 gas 计数器加伪指数函数，配置和需求路径保持不变：x_{t+1} = max(0, x_t + G_t − T_G)，b_t = fake_exponential(1, x_t, 8T_G)。计数器会保留 EIP-1559 取整丢掉的小额缺口，分母 8T_G 让它的响应速度与 EIP-1559 一致。

下表是两种更新规则在 4/5 比例下的对比，每格箭头前为 EIP-1559，箭头后为 EIP-4844 式：

传播时间 执行量（百万 gas） 状态增长（GiB/年） 近上限区块 平均基础费（wei）
3.0 秒 206.4 → 225.9 64.6 → 96.0 17.7% → 40.8% 22.3 → 6.6
3.5 秒 215.0 → 244.2 56.8 → 94.0 13.2% → 39.1% 18.3 → 3.6
4.0 秒 214.1 → 243.6 56.7 → 94.0 13.4% → 38.8% 18.8 → 3.7
4.5 秒 208.5 → 232.5 61.1 → 95.2 16.0% → 39.6% 21.5 → 5.4
5.0 秒 199.0 → 214.8 68.7 → 95.6 20.6% → 39.9% 27.2 → 10.5

费用接近均衡后，执行量和状态增长都回升了，但还剩两个问题。

拥堵大幅上升。 4/5 比例下上限只是目标的 1.25 倍。费用更低时，需求突发更容易顶到上限，38.8% 至 40.8% 的区块接近上限。

两条分支仍然都低于目标。 常规 gas 平均为目标的 85.8% 至 87.1%，归一化状态 gas 为 78.3% 至 80.0%。费用跟随每个区块中较大的那条分支，这条分支现在平均达到目标的 98.8% 至 100.0%；只要一条分支高于目标，另一条也得付更高的费用。一个费用能让较大的分支保持在目标上，但无法同时照顾两条。 在 1/2 比例下，同样更换更新规则几乎没有影响（执行量变化不到 150 万），因为那里的费用在 48 至 191 wei，取整很少起作用。

与 EIP-7999 对比

作者从上一篇帖子测试过的执行目标和数据目标中，为每种传播时间分配挑出两个 EIP-7999 配置：

  • 保守配置：位于执行与数据前沿之内、均衡执行费高于 1 wei、近上限区块占比不超过历史水平 4.73%（2026 年 2 月至 5 月的 860,505 个主网区块）的配置中，执行量最高的一个。
  • 最大吞吐配置：平均执行量最高的配置。

这里的保守规则比前几篇帖子的“历史锚定”规则更严格，后者允许近上限区块比历史占比多 20%，所以部分选择和数字略有不同。

EIP-7999 在所有配置中都把状态增长保持在每年 120 GiB 的目标上，下限调整加 EIP-8372 的各个变体只有 56.7 至 96.0 GiB。

拥堵相近且都较低时，EIP-7999 多交付 4% 至 34% 的执行量。 保守配置和 1/2 比例下的下限调整加 EIP-8372，近上限区块分别为 1.9% 至 4.4% 和 4.0% 至 4.5%，都接近或低于历史占比。在每种分配下，保守配置多交付 680 万至 5600 万执行 gas。

提高一维方案的目标比例，只能靠增加拥堵来缩小部分执行量差距。 在 4/5 时，下限调整加 EIP-8372 在 3 秒分配下比保守配置多 3280 万，3.5 秒下多 1700 万，更长的分配下则落后；但它有 13.2% 至 20.6% 的区块接近上限，保守配置只有 1.9% 至 4.4%。

拥堵更高时，EIP-7999 仍然交付更多。 最大吞吐配置比 4/5 比例的下限调整加 EIP-8372 多交付 4650 万至 7200 万执行量，近上限区块略多（16.6% 至 32.1%，对比 13.2% 至 20.6%）。与 EIP-4844 式变体相比，它们多交付 1950 万至 5620 万，近上限区块反而更少（16.6% 至 32.1%，对比 38.8% 至 40.8%）。

作者还检查了模拟过的每一次一维运行：上一篇的基线和下限调整加 EIP-8368 基准，五种目标比例下的下限调整加 EIP-8372，以及它的 EIP-4844 式变体，每种都覆盖五种传播时间分配。对每一次运行，同一分配下至少有一个位于执行与数据前沿之内的 EIP-7999 测试配置，执行量更多、状态增长保持在目标上、处于硬上限的区块占比不更高。最小的领先幅度是 680 万，出现在 1/2 比例、3 秒分配下的下限调整加 EIP-8372。

局限

需求标定。 结果依赖于用 2025 年 2 月和 7 月两次 gas 上限提高标定的需求模型，而测试的执行目标远超已观测到的需求。论文用这两次提高前后 21 天、60 天、75 天窗口估计的弹性做了稳健性检验。在每种标定下，基线和下限调整加 EIP-8368 基准里决定共享基础费的仍然是状态；为每种标定重新挑选目标的 EIP-7999，仍比下限调整加 EIP-8372 及其 EIP-4844 式变体交付更多执行量。领先幅度取决于标定，执行需求对价格越不敏感，领先通常越小。

只测了这些变体。 作者只测试了文中描述的一维变体，没有穷尽所有设计。论文还显示，当需求偏离标定值时，一次性标定的 EIP-8372 无法再让两条分支对齐；随需求变化重新标定缩放系数的机制，作者没有测试。

结论

提高目标比例和改进更新规则都能帮到一维机制，但各自带来新的代价。沿用 EIP-1559 更新时，更高的目标比例会压低状态增长、增加拥堵；EIP-4844 式更新恢复了状态增长，代价是让多得多的区块顶到上限。单一基础费跟随瓶颈资源，两种改动都无法让两项资源同时接近目标。作者的结论是：在标定的需求模型下，EIP-7999 交付更多执行量，状态增长保持在目标上，拥堵相近或更低，这支持以太坊在扩容中从“分开计量”转向“分开定价”。 关注 Glamsterdam 之后费用市场设计的读者，可以直接用作者的仓库复现这些模拟，并留意结论对需求标定的依赖。

原文

原文取自 ethresear.ch 帖子的 Markdown 源（/raw/26244）；原帖三张图已移到上方媒体区，正文中以 [Figure N] 标出原位置，图注保留在原位；数学公式保持原帖的 LaTeX 源文本；仅收录主楼。

More Meters or More Prices? One- vs. Multi-dimensional Fee Mechanisms on Ethereum

by Fei Wu. This work was partially conducted during my internship at the EF. I thank my mentor @misilva73 for helpful discussions and comments.

Overview

Previously, we have presented our analyses of the equilibrium and dynamic simulation of EIP-7999's multidimensional fee market, comparison with the post-Glamsterdam one-dimensional fee market. We combine and extend these analyses into a paper: More Meters or More Prices? One- vs. Multi-dimensional Fee Mechanisms on Ethereum.

In the previous post, we studied three one-dimensional benchmarks: the baseline (64-gas-per-byte floor and CPSB = 1530), floor-adjusted + EIP-8368, and floor-adjusted + EIP-8372. The strongest is floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 given the current resource demand, which we call the normalized benchmark in the paper: the transaction floor price is adjusted to each propagation allocation, and EIP-8372 scales CPSB and the state gas limit by a common factor, so that regular gas and state gas reach their targets at the same base fee in equilibrium. It keeps the EIP-1559 target-to-limit ratio of 1/2 and the EIP-1559 update rule. Under block-level demand variation, it delivers 151.9M–177.9M execution gas per block, but regular gas and normalized state gas both stay below their targets on average, giving 86.0–88.1 GiB/year of state growth against the 120 GiB/year target.

In the paper, we push this benchmark further. We first raise its target-to-limit ratio up to 4/5 to see whether it delivers more execution. The EIP-1559 update rule then turns out to be a constraint, because it cannot lower the base fee to the few-wei level that a high target requires. We then replace it with the fake-exponential update of EIP-4844. Finally, we compare these one-dimensional variants with EIP-7999. Throughout, we measure congestion as the share of near-limit blocks, whose gas usage reaches at least 98% of a hard limit. The results presented in this post can be reproduced from this repository.

Main results

  1. A higher target ratio for floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 delivers more execution, but contracts state growth and raises congestion. From 1/2 to 4/5, execution rises from 151.9M–177.9M to 199.0M–215.0M, but state growth falls from 86.0–88.1 to 56.7–68.7 GiB/year, and near-limit blocks rise from about 4% to 13.2%–20.6%. Under the EIP-1559 update, the base fee stays at 18–27 wei on average, far above its 2.4–7.2 wei equilibrium, and state, the most price-responsive resource, contracts the most.

  2. The EIP-1559 update rule prevents the fee from falling. The EIP-4844-style update allows lower fees and supports more execution/state, but brings more congestion. At a 4/5 ratio, execution rises to 214.8M–244.2M and state growth recovers to 94.0–96.0 GiB/year, but 38.8%–40.8% of blocks are near a limit, and regular gas and state gas both still stay below their targets.

  3. EIP-7999 delivers more execution with state growth at its target, at similar or lower congestion. At a similarly low share of near-limit blocks, the conservative EIP-7999 configurations deliver 4%–34% more execution than floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 at 1/2. Against the EIP-4844-style variant, the maximum-throughput configurations deliver 19.5M–56.2M more execution with fewer near-limit blocks.

Raising the target-to-limit ratio

We vary the target-to-limit ratio of floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 over 1/2, 3/5, 2/3, 3/4, and 4/5, keeping the gas limit and floor price of each propagation allocation. At each ratio, we recalibrate CPSB so that state usage at the target still corresponds to 120 GiB/year, and recompute the EIP-8372 scaling factor.

[Figure 1]

One-dimensional floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 benchmark under the EIP-1559 update, across target-to-limit ratios and propagation allocations. (a) Mean execution gas per block. (b) Annualized state growth, with the dashed line marking the 120 GiB/year target. Each point is the mean over the same 32 simulated demand paths.

Execution rises with the ratio at every allocation, reaching 199.0M–215.0M at 4/5. But state growth moves further away from its target, falling to 56.7–68.7 GiB/year, and blocks become more congested: at 4/5, 13.2%–20.6% of blocks are near a limit, against about 4% at 1/2.

The EIP-1559 update cannot lower the fee to its new equilibrium. A higher target clears at a much lower fee: at 4/5, the base fee at which both branches reach their targets is only 2.4–7.2 wei. Under EIP-1559, a block below the target lowers the base fee by

$$ \left\lfloor \frac{b_t,(T_G-G_t)}{8T_G}\right\rfloor, $$

where G_t is the gas usage of the larger branch. This decrease rounds to zero unless the block falls short of the target by at least 8/b_t of it. Once the fee is below 8 wei, no block can lower it, while every block above the target raises it by at least 1 wei. In the simulations, the fee never falls below 8 wei and averages 18.3–27.2 wei, about four to eight times its equilibrium value. In equilibrium, the 4/5 design would deliver 245M–280M of execution; in simulation, it delivers 199.0M–215.0M.

A fee above equilibrium contracts every resource, but state the most, because state is the most price-responsive resource. A higher ratio also lowers the per-block state byte limit relative to the target, from twice the target at 1/2 to 1.25 times at 4/5, which clips bursts of state creation.

Replacing the EIP-1559 update with an EIP-4844-style update

To let the fee reach these low levels, we replace the EIP-1559 update of floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 at a 4/5 ratio with the persistent excess-gas counter and fake exponential of EIP-4844, keeping the configurations and demand paths fixed:

$$ x_{t+1}=\max\left(0,;x_t+G_t-T_G\right), \qquad b_t=\mathtt{fake_exponential}\left(1,;x_t,;8T_G\right). $$

The counter keeps the small shortfalls that EIP-1559 rounds away, and the denominator 8T_G matches the response of EIP-1559. The table compares the two update rules at a 4/5 ratio. Each cell shows the EIP-1559 result followed by the EIP-4844-style result.

Propagation Execution (M) State growth (GiB/year) Near-limit blocks Mean base fee (wei)
3.0s 206.4 → 225.9 64.6 → 96.0 17.7% → 40.8% 22.3 → 6.6
3.5s 215.0 → 244.2 56.8 → 94.0 13.2% → 39.1% 18.3 → 3.6
4.0s 214.1 → 243.6 56.7 → 94.0 13.4% → 38.8% 18.8 → 3.7
4.5s 208.5 → 232.5 61.1 → 95.2 16.0% → 39.6% 21.5 → 5.4
5.0s 199.0 → 214.8 68.7 → 95.6 20.6% → 39.9% 27.2 → 10.5

With the EIP-4844-style update, the fee gets close to its equilibrium, so execution and state growth both recover. Two problems remain.

Congestion rises sharply. At a 4/5 ratio, the limit is only 1.25 times the target. With a lower fee, demand bursts reach the limit far more often, and 38.8%–40.8% of blocks are near a limit.

Both branches still stay below their targets. Regular gas averages 85.8%–87.1% of the target and normalized state gas 78.3%–80.0%. The fee follows the larger of the two branches in each block, which now averages 98.8%–100.0% of the target, so whenever one branch is above target, the other pays the higher fee as well. One fee can keep the larger branch on target, but not both. At a 1/2 ratio, the same change of update rule makes almost no difference (execution changes by less than 1.5M), because the fee there is 48–191 wei and rounding rarely matters.

Comparison with EIP-7999

We compare these one-dimensional variants with the two EIP-7999 selected configurations mentioned in the previous post, chosen from the tested execution and data targets at each propagation allocation:

  • Conservative: the highest-execution configuration inside the execution–data frontier, so that its equilibrium execution fee is above 1 wei, and whose share of near-limit blocks does not exceed the historical 4.73% (860,505 mainnet blocks from February to May 2026).
  • Maximum throughput: the configuration with the highest mean execution.

The conservative rule is stricter than the "historically anchored" rule of the previous posts, which allowed 20% more near-limit blocks than the historical share, so some selections and numbers differ slightly.

[Figure 2]

Mean execution gas per block of the one-dimensional floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 benchmark ("One-dimensional EIP-8372") at target-to-limit ratios of 1/2 and 4/5, and of the two EIP-7999 selections, under the same 32 demand paths. Labels are in millions of gas per block.

[Figure 3]

Share of near-limit blocks, whose gas usage reaches at least 98% of a hard limit, for the same designs and the EIP-4844-style variant of floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 at 4/5. The dashed line marks the historical share of 4.73% on mainnet from February to May 2026.

EIP-7999 keeps state growth at its 120 GiB/year target in every configuration, while the floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 variants deliver 56.7–96.0 GiB/year.

At similarly low congestion, EIP-7999 delivers 4%–34% more execution. The conservative configurations and floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 at 1/2 have 1.9%–4.4% and 4.0%–4.5% of blocks near a limit, both close to or below the historical share. The conservative configurations deliver 6.8M–56.0M more execution at every allocation.

A higher one-dimensional target ratio closes part of the execution gap only by raising congestion. At 4/5, floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 exceeds the conservative configurations by 32.8M at 3 seconds and 17.0M at 3.5 seconds and falls behind at longer allocations, but with 13.2%–20.6% of blocks near a limit, against 1.9%–4.4%.

At higher congestion, EIP-7999 still delivers more. The maximum-throughput configurations deliver 46.5M–72.0M more execution than floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 at 4/5, with somewhat more near-limit blocks (16.6%–32.1% against 13.2%–20.6%). Against the EIP-4844-style variant, they deliver 19.5M–56.2M more execution with fewer near-limit blocks (16.6%–32.1% against 38.8%–40.8%).

More generally, we checked every one-dimensional run we simulated: the baseline and floor-adjusted + EIP-8368 benchmarks of the previous post, floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 at the five target ratios, and its EIP-4844-style variant, each at five propagation allocations. For each run, at least one tested EIP-7999 configuration at the same allocation, inside the execution–data frontier, delivers more execution, keeps state growth at its target, and has no larger share of blocks at a hard limit. The smallest such margin is 6.8M, for floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 at 1/2 and 3 seconds.

Limitations

Demand calibration. The results are conditional on the demand model calibrated from the February and July 2025 gas-limit increases, and the tested execution targets extend well beyond observed demand. In the paper, we test robustness to elasticities estimated from 21-, 60-, and 75-day windows around these increases. Under every calibration, state still sets the shared base fee in the baseline and floor-adjusted + EIP-8368 benchmarks, and EIP-7999, with its targets reselected for each calibration, still delivers more execution than floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 and its EIP-4844-style variant. The size of the gain depends on the calibration and is generally smaller when execution demand is less price-responsive.

Tested variants only. We tested the one-dimensional variants described here, not every possible design. The paper also shows that a one-time EIP-8372 calibration no longer aligns the two branches when demand differs from the calibration, and we did not test a mechanism that recalibrates the scaling factor as demand changes.

Conclusion

Raising the target ratio and improving the update rule both help the one-dimensional mechanism, but each brings a new cost. Under the EIP-1559 update, a higher target ratio cuts state growth and raises congestion. The EIP-4844-style update recovers state growth only by letting far more blocks reach the limit. Because the one single base fee follows the bottleneck resource, neither change keeps both near their targets. Under the calibrated demand model, EIP-7999 delivers more execution with state growth at its target, at similar or lower congestion, which supports moving from separate metering to separate pricing as Ethereum scales.

{"version": 1, "original": {"title": "More Meters or More Prices? One- vs. Multi-dimensional Fee Mechanisms on Ethereum", "url": "https://ethresear.ch/t/more-meters-or-more-prices-one-vs-multi-dimensional-fee-mechanisms-on-ethereum/26244", "lang": "en", "html": "

More Meters or More Prices? One- vs. Multi-dimensional Fee Mechanisms on Ethereum

原文取自 ethresear.ch 帖子的 Markdown 源（/raw/26244）；原帖三张图已移到上方媒体区，正文中以 [Figure N] 标出原位置，图注保留在原位；数学公式保持原帖的 LaTeX 源文本；仅收录主楼。

by Fei Wu. This work was partially conducted during my internship at the EF. I thank my mentor @misilva73 for helpful discussions and comments.

Overview

Previously, we have presented our analyses of the equilibrium and dynamic simulation of EIP-7999's multidimensional fee market, comparison with the post-Glamsterdam one-dimensional fee market. We combine and extend these analyses into a paper: More Meters or More Prices? One- vs. Multi-dimensional Fee Mechanisms on Ethereum.

In the previous post, we studied three one-dimensional benchmarks: the baseline (64-gas-per-byte floor and CPSB = 1530), floor-adjusted + EIP-8368, and floor-adjusted + EIP-8372. The strongest is floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 given the current resource demand, which we call the normalized benchmark in the paper: the transaction floor price is adjusted to each propagation allocation, and EIP-8372 scales CPSB and the state gas limit by a common factor, so that regular gas and state gas reach their targets at the same base fee in equilibrium. It keeps the EIP-1559 target-to-limit ratio of 1/2 and the EIP-1559 update rule. Under block-level demand variation, it delivers 151.9M–177.9M execution gas per block, but regular gas and normalized state gas both stay below their targets on average, giving 86.0–88.1 GiB/year of state growth against the 120 GiB/year target.

In the paper, we push this benchmark further. We first raise its target-to-limit ratio up to 4/5 to see whether it delivers more execution. The EIP-1559 update rule then turns out to be a constraint, because it cannot lower the base fee to the few-wei level that a high target requires. We then replace it with the fake-exponential update of EIP-4844. Finally, we compare these one-dimensional variants with EIP-7999. Throughout, we measure congestion as the share of near-limit blocks, whose gas usage reaches at least 98% of a hard limit. The results presented in this post can be reproduced from this repository.

Main results

  1. A higher target ratio for floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 delivers more execution, but contracts state growth and raises congestion. From 1/2 to 4/5, execution rises from 151.9M–177.9M to 199.0M–215.0M, but state growth falls from 86.0–88.1 to 56.7–68.7 GiB/year, and near-limit blocks rise from about 4% to 13.2%–20.6%. Under the EIP-1559 update, the base fee stays at 18–27 wei on average, far above its 2.4–7.2 wei equilibrium, and state, the most price-responsive resource, contracts the most.

  2. The EIP-1559 update rule prevents the fee from falling. The EIP-4844-style update allows lower fees and supports more execution/state, but brings more congestion. At a 4/5 ratio, execution rises to 214.8M–244.2M and state growth recovers to 94.0–96.0 GiB/year, but 38.8%–40.8% of blocks are near a limit, and regular gas and state gas both still stay below their targets.

  3. EIP-7999 delivers more execution with state growth at its target, at similar or lower congestion. At a similarly low share of near-limit blocks, the conservative EIP-7999 configurations deliver 4%–34% more execution than floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 at 1/2. Against the EIP-4844-style variant, the maximum-throughput configurations deliver 19.5M–56.2M more execution with fewer near-limit blocks.

Raising the target-to-limit ratio

We vary the target-to-limit ratio of floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 over 1/2, 3/5, 2/3, 3/4, and 4/5, keeping the gas limit and floor price of each propagation allocation. At each ratio, we recalibrate CPSB so that state usage at the target still corresponds to 120 GiB/year, and recompute the EIP-8372 scaling factor.

[Figure 1]

One-dimensional floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 benchmark under the EIP-1559 update, across target-to-limit ratios and propagation allocations. (a) Mean execution gas per block. (b) Annualized state growth, with the dashed line marking the 120 GiB/year target. Each point is the mean over the same 32 simulated demand paths.

Execution rises with the ratio at every allocation, reaching 199.0M–215.0M at 4/5. But state growth moves further away from its target, falling to 56.7–68.7 GiB/year, and blocks become more congested: at 4/5, 13.2%–20.6% of blocks are near a limit, against about 4% at 1/2.

The EIP-1559 update cannot lower the fee to its new equilibrium. A higher target clears at a much lower fee: at 4/5, the base fee at which both branches reach their targets is only 2.4–7.2 wei. Under EIP-1559, a block below the target lowers the base fee by

$$ \left\lfloor \frac{b_t,(T_G-G_t)}{8T_G}\right\rfloor, $$

where G_t is the gas usage of the larger branch. This decrease rounds to zero unless the block falls short of the target by at least 8/b_t of it. Once the fee is below 8 wei, no block can lower it, while every block above the target raises it by at least 1 wei. In the simulations, the fee never falls below 8 wei and averages 18.3–27.2 wei, about four to eight times its equilibrium value. In equilibrium, the 4/5 design would deliver 245M–280M of execution; in simulation, it delivers 199.0M–215.0M.

A fee above equilibrium contracts every resource, but state the most, because state is the most price-responsive resource. A higher ratio also lowers the per-block state byte limit relative to the target, from twice the target at 1/2 to 1.25 times at 4/5, which clips bursts of state creation.

Replacing the EIP-1559 update with an EIP-4844-style update

To let the fee reach these low levels, we replace the EIP-1559 update of floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 at a 4/5 ratio with the persistent excess-gas counter and fake exponential of EIP-4844, keeping the configurations and demand paths fixed:

$$ x_{t+1}=\max\left(0,;x_t+G_t-T_G\right), \qquad b_t=\mathtt{fake_exponential}\left(1,;x_t,;8T_G\right). $$

The counter keeps the small shortfalls that EIP-1559 rounds away, and the denominator 8T_G matches the response of EIP-1559. The table compares the two update rules at a 4/5 ratio. Each cell shows the EIP-1559 result followed by the EIP-4844-style result.

Propagation Execution (M) State growth (GiB/year) Near-limit blocks Mean base fee (wei)
3.0s 206.4 → 225.9 64.6 → 96.0 17.7% → 40.8% 22.3 → 6.6
3.5s 215.0 → 244.2 56.8 → 94.0 13.2% → 39.1% 18.3 → 3.6
4.0s 214.1 → 243.6 56.7 → 94.0 13.4% → 38.8% 18.8 → 3.7
4.5s 208.5 → 232.5 61.1 → 95.2 16.0% → 39.6% 21.5 → 5.4
5.0s 199.0 → 214.8 68.7 → 95.6 20.6% → 39.9% 27.2 → 10.5

With the EIP-4844-style update, the fee gets close to its equilibrium, so execution and state growth both recover. Two problems remain.

Congestion rises sharply. At a 4/5 ratio, the limit is only 1.25 times the target. With a lower fee, demand bursts reach the limit far more often, and 38.8%–40.8% of blocks are near a limit.

Both branches still stay below their targets. Regular gas averages 85.8%–87.1% of the target and normalized state gas 78.3%–80.0%. The fee follows the larger of the two branches in each block, which now averages 98.8%–100.0% of the target, so whenever one branch is above target, the other pays the higher fee as well. One fee can keep the larger branch on target, but not both. At a 1/2 ratio, the same change of update rule makes almost no difference (execution changes by less than 1.5M), because the fee there is 48–191 wei and rounding rarely matters.

Comparison with EIP-7999

We compare these one-dimensional variants with the two EIP-7999 selected configurations mentioned in the previous post, chosen from the tested execution and data targets at each propagation allocation:

  • Conservative: the highest-execution configuration inside the execution–data frontier, so that its equilibrium execution fee is above 1 wei, and whose share of near-limit blocks does not exceed the historical 4.73% (860,505 mainnet blocks from February to May 2026).
  • Maximum throughput: the configuration with the highest mean execution.

The conservative rule is stricter than the "historically anchored" rule of the previous posts, which allowed 20% more near-limit blocks than the historical share, so some selections and numbers differ slightly.

[Figure 2]

Mean execution gas per block of the one-dimensional floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 benchmark ("One-dimensional EIP-8372") at target-to-limit ratios of 1/2 and 4/5, and of the two EIP-7999 selections, under the same 32 demand paths. Labels are in millions of gas per block.

[Figure 3]

Share of near-limit blocks, whose gas usage reaches at least 98% of a hard limit, for the same designs and the EIP-4844-style variant of floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 at 4/5. The dashed line marks the historical share of 4.73% on mainnet from February to May 2026.

EIP-7999 keeps state growth at its 120 GiB/year target in every configuration, while the floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 variants deliver 56.7–96.0 GiB/year.

At similarly low congestion, EIP-7999 delivers 4%–34% more execution. The conservative configurations and floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 at 1/2 have 1.9%–4.4% and 4.0%–4.5% of blocks near a limit, both close to or below the historical share. The conservative configurations deliver 6.8M–56.0M more execution at every allocation.

A higher one-dimensional target ratio closes part of the execution gap only by raising congestion. At 4/5, floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 exceeds the conservative configurations by 32.8M at 3 seconds and 17.0M at 3.5 seconds and falls behind at longer allocations, but with 13.2%–20.6% of blocks near a limit, against 1.9%–4.4%.

At higher congestion, EIP-7999 still delivers more. The maximum-throughput configurations deliver 46.5M–72.0M more execution than floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 at 4/5, with somewhat more near-limit blocks (16.6%–32.1% against 13.2%–20.6%). Against the EIP-4844-style variant, they deliver 19.5M–56.2M more execution with fewer near-limit blocks (16.6%–32.1% against 38.8%–40.8%).

More generally, we checked every one-dimensional run we simulated: the baseline and floor-adjusted + EIP-8368 benchmarks of the previous post, floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 at the five target ratios, and its EIP-4844-style variant, each at five propagation allocations. For each run, at least one tested EIP-7999 configuration at the same allocation, inside the execution–data frontier, delivers more execution, keeps state growth at its target, and has no larger share of blocks at a hard limit. The smallest such margin is 6.8M, for floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 at 1/2 and 3 seconds.

Limitations

Demand calibration. The results are conditional on the demand model calibrated from the February and July 2025 gas-limit increases, and the tested execution targets extend well beyond observed demand. In the paper, we test robustness to elasticities estimated from 21-, 60-, and 75-day windows around these increases. Under every calibration, state still sets the shared base fee in the baseline and floor-adjusted + EIP-8368 benchmarks, and EIP-7999, with its targets reselected for each calibration, still delivers more execution than floor-adjusted + EIP-8372 and its EIP-4844-style variant. The size of the gain depends on the calibration and is generally smaller when execution demand is less price-responsive.

Tested variants only. We tested the one-dimensional variants described here, not every possible design. The paper also shows that a one-time EIP-8372 calibration no longer aligns the two branches when demand differs from the calibration, and we did not test a mechanism that recalibrates the scaling factor as demand changes.

Conclusion

Raising the target ratio and improving the update rule both help the one-dimensional mechanism, but each brings a new cost. Under the EIP-1559 update, a higher target ratio cuts state growth and raises congestion. The EIP-4844-style update recovers state growth only by letting far more blocks reach the limit. Because the one single base fee follows the bottleneck resource, neither change keeps both near their targets. Under the calibrated demand model, EIP-7999 delivers more execution with state growth at its target, at similar or lower congestion, which supports moving from separate metering to separate pricing as Ethereum scales.

相关链接：https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33455

One- vs. Multi-dimensional Fee Mechanisms on Ethereum》（arXiv 2610.33455）。帖中结果可以用作者公开的代码仓库复现。 ## 起点：最强的一维基准，仍有两项资源达不到目标 上一篇帖子比较了三个一维基准：基线方案（每字节 64 gas 的下限，`CPSB = 1530`）、下限调整加 EIP-8368、下限调整加 EIP-8372。按当前的资源需求，最强的是**下限调整加 EIP-8372**，论文称之为“归一化基准”。它的做法是：交易下限价格随每种传播时间分配（propagation allocation）调整；EIP-8372 把 `CPSB` 和状态 gas 上限按同一个系数缩放，让常规 gas 和状态 gas 在均衡时于同一个基础费下达到各自目标。它保留 EIP-1559 的目标与上限之比 1/2，也保留 EIP-1559 的更新规则。 在区块层面的需求波动下，这个基准每个区块交付 1.519 亿至 1.779 亿执行 gas，但常规 gas 和归一化后的状态 gas 平均都低于目标，状态增长为每年 86.0 至 88.1 GiB，目标是 120 GiB。 论文在此基础上继续推进：先把目标与上限之比提高到最多 4/5，看能否交付更多执行量；发现 EIP-1559 的更新规则成了约束后，换成 EIP-4844 的伪指数（fake exponential）更新；最后与 EIP-7999 比较。全文用**近上限区块**的占比衡量拥堵，指 gas 用量达到某个硬上限 98% 以上的区块。 ## 提高目标比例：执行量上去了，状态增长和拥堵变差 作者把下限调整加 EIP-8372 的目标与上限之比依次设为 1/2、3/5、2/3、3/4、4/5，每种传播时间分配下的 gas 上限和下限价格不变。每个比例下都重新标定 `CPSB`，让达到目标时的状态用量仍对应每年 120 GiB，并重新计算 EIP-8372 的缩放系数。 ![Figure 1]() 每种分配下，执行量都随比例上升，到 4/5 时达到 1.990 亿至 2.150 亿。代价是状态增长离目标更远，降到每年 56.7 至 68.7 GiB；区块也更拥堵，4/5 时有 13.2% 至 20.6% 的区块接近上限，1/2 时约为 4%。 **原因在于 EIP-1559 的更新规则无法把费用降到新的均衡点。** 目标越高，出清的费用越低：在 4/5 时，两条分支同时达到目标的基础费只有 2.4 至 7.2 wei。按 EIP-1559，一个低于目标的区块会把基础费降低 ⌊b_t(T_G − G_t) / 8T_G⌋，其中 G_t 是两条分支中用量较大的那一条。除非区块比目标少出至少 8/b_t 的比例，这个降幅都会被取整成零。费用一旦低于 8 wei，任何区块都无法再让它下降，而每个高于目标的区块都会让它至少涨 1 wei。 模拟中费用从未低于 8 wei，平均为 18.3 至 27.2 wei，是均衡值的四到八倍。按均衡计算，4/5 的设计本应交付 2.45 亿至 2.80 亿执行量，模拟中只有 1.990 亿至 2.150 亿。 费用高于均衡会压缩所有资源，状态被压得最多，因为它对价格最敏感。比例提高还降低了每块状态字节上限相对目标的倍数，从 1/2 时的 2 倍降到 4/5 时的 1.25 倍，状态创建的突发会被截断。 ## 换成 EIP-4844 式更新：费用降下来了，拥堵翻倍 为了让费用能降到这么低，作者在 4/5 比例下把 EIP-1559 更新换成 EIP-4844 的持续超额 gas 计数器加伪指数函数，配置和需求路径保持不变：x_{t+1} = max(0, x_t + G_t − T_G)，b_t = fake_exponential(1, x_t, 8T_G)。计数器会保留 EIP-1559 取整丢掉的小额缺口，分母 8T_G 让它的响应速度与 EIP-1559 一致。 下表是两种更新规则在 4/5 比例下的对比，每格箭头前为 EIP-1559，箭头后为 EIP-4844 式： | 传播时间 | 执行量（百万 gas） | 状态增长（GiB/年） | 近上限区块 | 平均基础费（wei） | |----|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 3.0 秒 | 206.4 → 225.9 | 64.6 → 96.0 | 17.7% → 40.8% | 22.3 → 6.6 | | 3.5 秒 | 215.0 → 244.2 | 56.8 → 94.0 | 13.2% → 39.1% | 18.3 → 3.6 | | 4.0 秒 | 214.1 → 243.6 | 56.7 → 94.0 | 13.4% → 38.8% | 18.8 → 3.7 | | 4.5 秒 | 208.5 → 232.5 | 61.1 → 95.2 | 16.0% → 39.6% | 21.5 → 5.4 | | 5.0 秒 | 199.0 → 214.8 | 68.7 → 95.6 | 20.6% → 39.9% | 27.2 → 10.5 | 费用接近均衡后，执行量和状态增长都回升了，但还剩两个问题。 **拥堵大幅上升。** 4/5 比例下上限只是目标的 1.25 倍。费用更低时，需求突发更容易顶到上限，38.8% 至 40.8% 的区块接近上限。 **两条分支仍然都低于目标。** 常规 gas 平均为目标的 85.8% 至 87.1%，归一化状态 gas 为 78.3% 至 80.0%。费用跟随每个区块中较大的那条分支，这条分支现在平均达到目标的 98.8% 至 100.0%；只要一条分支高于目标，另一条也得付更高的费用。**一个费用能让较大的分支保持在目标上，但无法同时照顾两条。** 在 1/2 比例下，同样更换更新规则几乎没有影响（执行量变化不到 150 万），因为那里的费用在 48 至 191 wei，取整很少起作用。 ## 与 EIP-7999 对比 作者从上一篇帖子测试过的执行目标和数据目标中，为每种传播时间分配挑出两个 EIP-7999 配置： - **保守配置**：位于执行与数据前沿之内、均衡执行费高于 1 wei、近上限区块占比不超过历史水平 4.73%（2026 年 2 月至 5 月的 860,505 个主网区块）的配置中，执行量最高的一个。 - **最大吞吐配置**：平均执行量最高的配置。 这里的保守规则比前几篇帖子的“历史锚定”规则更严格，后者允许近上限区块比历史占比多 20%，所以部分选择和数字略有不同。 ![Figure 2]() ![fig3\_near\_limit\_comparison]() EIP-7999 在所有配置中都把状态增长保持在每年 120 GiB 的目标上，下限调整加 EIP-8372 的各个变体只有 56.7 至 96.0 GiB。 **拥堵相近且都较低时，EIP-7999 多交付 4% 至 34% 的执行量。** 保守配置和 1/2 比例下的下限调整加 EIP-8372，近上限区块分别为 1.9% 至 4.4% 和 4.0% 至 4.5%，都接近或低于历史占比。在每种分配下，保守配置多交付 680 万至 5600 万执行 gas。 **提高一维方案的目标比例，只能靠增加拥堵来缩小部分执行量差距。** 在 4/5 时，下限调整加 EIP-8372 在 3 秒分配下比保守配置多 3280 万，3.5 秒下多 1700 万，更长的分配下则落后；但它有 13.2% 至 20.6% 的区块接近上限，保守配置只有 1.9% 至 4.4%。 **拥堵更高时，EIP-7999 仍然交付更多。** 最大吞吐配置比 4/5 比例的下限调整加 EIP-8372 多交付 4650 万至 7200 万执行量，近上限区块略多（16.6% 至 32.1%，对比 13.2% 至 20.6%）。与 EIP-4844 式变体相比，它们多交付 1950 万至 5620 万，近上限区块反而更少（16.6% 至 32.1%，对比 38.8% 至 40.8%）。 作者还检查了模拟过的每一次一维运行：上一篇的基线和下限调整加 EIP-8368 基准，五种目标比例下的下限调整加 EIP-8372，以及它的 EIP-4844 式变体，每种都覆盖五种传播时间分配。对每一次运行，同一分配下至少有一个位于执行与数据前沿之内的 EIP-7999 测试配置，执行量更多、状态增长保持在目标上、处于硬上限的区块占比不更高。最小的领先幅度是 680 万，出现在 1/2 比例、3 秒分配下的下限调整加 EIP-8372。 ## 局限 **需求标定。** 结果依赖于用 2025 年 2 月和 7 月两次 gas 上限提高标定的需求模型，而测试的执行目标远超已观测到的需求。论文用这两次提高前后 21 天、60 天、75 天窗口估计的弹性做了稳健性检验。在每种标定下，基线和下限调整加 EIP-8368 基准里决定共享基础费的仍然是状态；为每种标定重新挑选目标的 EIP-7999，仍比下限调整加 EIP-8372 及其 EIP-4844 式变体交付更多执行量。领先幅度取决于标定，执行需求对价格越不敏感，领先通常越小。 **只测了这些变体。** 作者只测试了文中描述的一维变体，没有穷尽所有设计。论文还显示，当需求偏离标定值时，一次性标定的 EIP-8372 无法再让两条分支对齐；随需求变化重新标定缩放系数的机制，作者没有测试。 ## 结论 提高目标比例和改进更新规则都能帮到一维机制，但各自带来新的代价。沿用 EIP-1559 更新时，更高的目标比例会压低状态增长、增加拥堵；EIP-4844 式更新恢复了状态增长，代价是让多得多的区块顶到上限。单一基础费跟随瓶颈资源，两种改动都无法让两项资源同时接近目标。作者的结论是：**在标定的需求模型下，EIP-7999 交付更多执行量，状态增长保持在目标上，拥堵相近或更低，这支持以太坊在扩容中从“分开计量”转向“分开定价”。** 关注 Glamsterdam 之后费用市场设计的读者，可以直接用作者的仓库复现这些模拟，并留意结论对需求标定的依赖。", "html": "

在以太坊上，把执行 gas 和状态增长放在同一个基础费（base fee）下定价，会出现一个问题：费用只能追着更紧的那项资源走。Fei Wu 在 ethresear.ch 发布的新帖用模拟数据对比了两条路线：继续改进一维费用机制，或者转向 EIP-7999 的多维定价。在标定的需求模型下，EIP-7999 在拥堵相近或更低的情况下交付更多执行量，同时把状态增长保持在每年 120 GiB 的目标上。

这项工作部分完成于作者在以太坊基金会（EF）实习期间，作者感谢导师 misilva73 的讨论和意见。帖子把此前三篇分析（EIP-7999 多维费用市场的均衡分析、动态模拟，以及与 Glamsterdam 之后一维费用市场的对比）合并扩展成一篇论文：《More Meters or More Prices? One- vs. Multi-dimensional Fee Mechanisms on Ethereum》（arXiv 2610.33455）。帖中结果可以用作者公开的代码仓库复现。

起点：最强的一维基准，仍有两项资源达不到目标

上一篇帖子比较了三个一维基准：基线方案（每字节 64 gas 的下限，CPSB = 1530）、下限调整加 EIP-8368、下限调整加 EIP-8372。按当前的资源需求，最强的是下限调整加 EIP-8372，论文称之为“归一化基准”。它的做法是：交易下限价格随每种传播时间分配（propagation allocation）调整；EIP-8372 把 CPSB 和状态 gas 上限按同一个系数缩放，让常规 gas 和状态 gas 在均衡时于同一个基础费下达到各自目标。它保留 EIP-1559 的目标与上限之比 1/2，也保留 EIP-1559 的更新规则。

在区块层面的需求波动下，这个基准每个区块交付 1.519 亿至 1.779 亿执行 gas，但常规 gas 和归一化后的状态 gas 平均都低于目标，状态增长为每年 86.0 至 88.1 GiB，目标是 120 GiB。

论文在此基础上继续推进：先把目标与上限之比提高到最多 4/5，看能否交付更多执行量；发现 EIP-1559 的更新规则成了约束后，换成 EIP-4844 的伪指数（fake exponential）更新；最后与 EIP-7999 比较。全文用近上限区块的占比衡量拥堵，指 gas 用量达到某个硬上限 98% 以上的区块。

提高目标比例：执行量上去了，状态增长和拥堵变差

作者把下限调整加 EIP-8372 的目标与上限之比依次设为 1/2、3/5、2/3、3/4、4/5，每种传播时间分配下的 gas 上限和下限价格不变。每个比例下都重新标定 CPSB，让达到目标时的状态用量仍对应每年 120 GiB，并重新计算 EIP-8372 的缩放系数。

每种分配下，执行量都随比例上升，到 4/5 时达到 1.990 亿至 2.150 亿。代价是状态增长离目标更远，降到每年 56.7 至 68.7 GiB；区块也更拥堵，4/5 时有 13.2% 至 20.6% 的区块接近上限，1/2 时约为 4%。

原因在于 EIP-1559 的更新规则无法把费用降到新的均衡点。 目标越高，出清的费用越低：在 4/5 时，两条分支同时达到目标的基础费只有 2.4 至 7.2 wei。按 EIP-1559，一个低于目标的区块会把基础费降低 ⌊b_t(T_G − G_t) / 8T_G⌋，其中 G_t 是两条分支中用量较大的那一条。除非区块比目标少出至少 8/b_t 的比例，这个降幅都会被取整成零。费用一旦低于 8 wei，任何区块都无法再让它下降，而每个高于目标的区块都会让它至少涨 1 wei。

模拟中费用从未低于 8 wei，平均为 18.3 至 27.2 wei，是均衡值的四到八倍。按均衡计算，4/5 的设计本应交付 2.45 亿至 2.80 亿执行量，模拟中只有 1.990 亿至 2.150 亿。

费用高于均衡会压缩所有资源，状态被压得最多，因为它对价格最敏感。比例提高还降低了每块状态字节上限相对目标的倍数，从 1/2 时的 2 倍降到 4/5 时的 1.25 倍，状态创建的突发会被截断。

换成 EIP-4844 式更新：费用降下来了，拥堵翻倍

为了让费用能降到这么低，作者在 4/5 比例下把 EIP-1559 更新换成 EIP-4844 的持续超额 gas 计数器加伪指数函数，配置和需求路径保持不变：x_{t+1} = max(0, x_t + G_t − T_G)，b_t = fake_exponential(1, x_t, 8T_G)。计数器会保留 EIP-1559 取整丢掉的小额缺口，分母 8T_G 让它的响应速度与 EIP-1559 一致。

下表是两种更新规则在 4/5 比例下的对比，每格箭头前为 EIP-1559，箭头后为 EIP-4844 式：

传播时间 执行量（百万 gas） 状态增长（GiB/年） 近上限区块 平均基础费（wei）
3.0 秒 206.4 → 225.9 64.6 → 96.0 17.7% → 40.8% 22.3 → 6.6
3.5 秒 215.0 → 244.2 56.8 → 94.0 13.2% → 39.1% 18.3 → 3.6
4.0 秒 214.1 → 243.6 56.7 → 94.0 13.4% → 38.8% 18.8 → 3.7
4.5 秒 208.5 → 232.5 61.1 → 95.2 16.0% → 39.6% 21.5 → 5.4
5.0 秒 199.0 → 214.8 68.7 → 95.6 20.6% → 39.9% 27.2 → 10.5

费用接近均衡后，执行量和状态增长都回升了，但还剩两个问题。

拥堵大幅上升。 4/5 比例下上限只是目标的 1.25 倍。费用更低时，需求突发更容易顶到上限，38.8% 至 40.8% 的区块接近上限。

两条分支仍然都低于目标。 常规 gas 平均为目标的 85.8% 至 87.1%，归一化状态 gas 为 78.3% 至 80.0%。费用跟随每个区块中较大的那条分支，这条分支现在平均达到目标的 98.8% 至 100.0%；只要一条分支高于目标，另一条也得付更高的费用。一个费用能让较大的分支保持在目标上，但无法同时照顾两条。 在 1/2 比例下，同样更换更新规则几乎没有影响（执行量变化不到 150 万），因为那里的费用在 48 至 191 wei，取整很少起作用。

与 EIP-7999 对比

作者从上一篇帖子测试过的执行目标和数据目标中，为每种传播时间分配挑出两个 EIP-7999 配置：

  • 保守配置：位于执行与数据前沿之内、均衡执行费高于 1 wei、近上限区块占比不超过历史水平 4.73%（2026 年 2 月至 5 月的 860,505 个主网区块）的配置中，执行量最高的一个。
  • 最大吞吐配置：平均执行量最高的配置。

这里的保守规则比前几篇帖子的“历史锚定”规则更严格，后者允许近上限区块比历史占比多 20%，所以部分选择和数字略有不同。

EIP-7999 在所有配置中都把状态增长保持在每年 120 GiB 的目标上，下限调整加 EIP-8372 的各个变体只有 56.7 至 96.0 GiB。

拥堵相近且都较低时，EIP-7999 多交付 4% 至 34% 的执行量。 保守配置和 1/2 比例下的下限调整加 EIP-8372，近上限区块分别为 1.9% 至 4.4% 和 4.0% 至 4.5%，都接近或低于历史占比。在每种分配下，保守配置多交付 680 万至 5600 万执行 gas。

提高一维方案的目标比例，只能靠增加拥堵来缩小部分执行量差距。 在 4/5 时，下限调整加 EIP-8372 在 3 秒分配下比保守配置多 3280 万，3.5 秒下多 1700 万，更长的分配下则落后；但它有 13.2% 至 20.6% 的区块接近上限，保守配置只有 1.9% 至 4.4%。

拥堵更高时，EIP-7999 仍然交付更多。 最大吞吐配置比 4/5 比例的下限调整加 EIP-8372 多交付 4650 万至 7200 万执行量，近上限区块略多（16.6% 至 32.1%，对比 13.2% 至 20.6%）。与 EIP-4844 式变体相比，它们多交付 1950 万至 5620 万，近上限区块反而更少（16.6% 至 32.1%，对比 38.8% 至 40.8%）。

作者还检查了模拟过的每一次一维运行：上一篇的基线和下限调整加 EIP-8368 基准，五种目标比例下的下限调整加 EIP-8372，以及它的 EIP-4844 式变体，每种都覆盖五种传播时间分配。对每一次运行，同一分配下至少有一个位于执行与数据前沿之内的 EIP-7999 测试配置，执行量更多、状态增长保持在目标上、处于硬上限的区块占比不更高。最小的领先幅度是 680 万，出现在 1/2 比例、3 秒分配下的下限调整加 EIP-8372。

局限

需求标定。 结果依赖于用 2025 年 2 月和 7 月两次 gas 上限提高标定的需求模型，而测试的执行目标远超已观测到的需求。论文用这两次提高前后 21 天、60 天、75 天窗口估计的弹性做了稳健性检验。在每种标定下，基线和下限调整加 EIP-8368 基准里决定共享基础费的仍然是状态；为每种标定重新挑选目标的 EIP-7999，仍比下限调整加 EIP-8372 及其 EIP-4844 式变体交付更多执行量。领先幅度取决于标定，执行需求对价格越不敏感，领先通常越小。

只测了这些变体。 作者只测试了文中描述的一维变体，没有穷尽所有设计。论文还显示，当需求偏离标定值时，一次性标定的 EIP-8372 无法再让两条分支对齐；随需求变化重新标定缩放系数的机制，作者没有测试。

结论

提高目标比例和改进更新规则都能帮到一维机制，但各自带来新的代价。沿用 EIP-1559 更新时，更高的目标比例会压低状态增长、增加拥堵；EIP-4844 式更新恢复了状态增长，代价是让多得多的区块顶到上限。单一基础费跟随瓶颈资源，两种改动都无法让两项资源同时接近目标。作者的结论是：在标定的需求模型下，EIP-7999 交付更多执行量，状态增长保持在目标上，拥堵相近或更低，这支持以太坊在扩容中从“分开计量”转向“分开定价”。 关注 Glamsterdam 之后费用市场设计的读者，可以直接用作者的仓库复现这些模拟，并留意结论对需求标定的依赖。

item.title: IBM 发布 LLMON：用特殊 token 把指令和数据分开，Granite 4.1 预览模型抵御提示注入
item.author: Abraham Daniels, Basel Shbita, Chad DeLuca, Dan Gutfreund, Michael Hind, Shub A (IBM Granite)
item.description:
IBM Granite 团队推出面向大模型的标记语言 LLMON 和两个 Granite 4.1 预览模型：结构分隔符改用保留 token，exec 块绑定指令与数据；团队称在 OPI 基准上比所测最好的前沿模型多挡住 47% 的注入攻击，通用能力与 Instruct 版持平，仍是实验性预览。

中文改写

大语言模型靠上下文生成下一批 token。在一段很长的交互里，上下文会塞满各种成分：系统提示、过去的对话轮次、作用于检索文档的指令、工具返回或用户数据、限制输出的要求，以及推理链。IBM Granite 团队在 Hugging Face 博客上指出，这些成分本来有丰富的结构，但大多要么只是隐含在模型里，要么用 JSON 这类并非为大模型设计的格式表达。团队认为，这是大模型（尤其是较小的模型）脆弱、会以意想不到的方式出错的主要原因之一；结构不明确也会被攻击者利用，比如提示注入。

为此，团队开发了 LLMON（LLM Object Notation，读作 “lemon”），一种面向大模型的原生标记语言，用来把结构和语义明确地告诉模型。语义上连贯的成分用有意义的标签标记，标签外面包着保留的特殊 token 分隔符。数据模式（包括嵌套）以因果语言模型不会误解的方式写明。每个块有唯一 ID，可以指向上下文中任意位置的某条指令，并把它绑定到该指令要处理的数据上，类似编程语言里调用函数并传入参数。

团队同时发布了两个基于 Granite 4.1 基础模型、经训练可以读写 LLMON 标记文本的实验性预览模型：granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview 和 granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview，以及一个 GitHub 仓库，内含处理 LLMON 的工具包和工作流、模板示例。

团队给出的四项用途

  • 抵御间接提示注入。 藏在用户数据里的注入指令，大多会被 LLMON 模型忽略，因为指令和数据是明确分开的。在部分基准上攻击成功率降到接近零，而常规指令微调模型被劫持的概率很高。团队称这是在保持与 Granite 4.1 Instruct 模型相当的通用能力的前提下做到的。
  • 不串味。 每条指令都绑定到它要处理的确切数据，无关段落、旧的对话轮次和工具输出不会被拉进答案。
  • 应用代码里的结构可以被模型利用。 指令、数据和要求都有清楚的标记。可以在 Mellea 里试用，它会自动把大模型调用转成 LLMON，原生支持这种格式。
  • 不用再逼模型遵守 JSON 结构。 团队提供的转换器可以把现有 JSON 无损转成 LLMON；也可以自定义结构和标签，在 LLMON 模型上微调一个 LoRA 来理解它们。

为什么不用 JSON

JSON 是为解析器设计的，不是为因果语言模型设计的。分词器不受语法约束，而结构是靠 {、"、: 这些在普通文本里也会出现的 token 表达的。在模型眼里，文档里的一个引号和结束一个字段的引号是同一个 token。解析器眼中清清楚楚的转义规则，在模型那里只是统计规律。嵌套深度靠数括号来体现，而 Transformer 在这方面已知较弱，跨度越长越明显。

LLMON 是一种类 XML 的标记，它的结构分隔符是保留的特殊 token 而不是字符，因此结构和内容使用词表中互不重叠的部分。标签写在每个片段的开头，片段之间的边界是明确的。嵌套结构在局部写明，模型不必在长跨度上记住层级关系。

考虑到多数团队已有基于 JSON 的流水线，团队提供了转换工具和示例 notebook，可以在 JSON 和 LLMON 之间无损互转。

与对话模板的关系：在角色之外再标出“每一块是什么”

LLMON 不替代对话模板（chat template），它在对话模板之上补充信息。常规对话模板告诉模型哪部分属于哪个角色（system、user、assistant）；LLMON 还告诉模型每个成分是什么意思，以及成分之间在角色内、跨角色的关系。

预览模型自带对话模板，开发者照常构造传给任何对话模型的 messages 列表，再照常调用 apply_chat_template。唯一的区别是，一个轮次可以给自己的各部分命名，并把每部分标为 exec: True 或 False。标为 True 的部分会被绑定进渲染结果底部的 exec 块，这个块写明要执行哪条指令、作用于什么；标为 False 的部分仍会渲染进上下文，但没有任何地方引用它。博客给出的例子是：

messages = [ { "role": "user",
               "instruction": [{ "value": "Write a short paragraph about", "exec": True }],
               "data": [{ "value": "IBM Company", "exec": True }],
               "requirement": [ {"value": "Use less than 10 words", "exec": True},
                                {"value": "Do not use commas", "exec": True}]
             } ]

模型实际收到的是下面这段（为便于阅读加了换行和缩进，模板本身不输出这些）：

<|open|>instr<|:|>»ñ<|close|>Write a short paragraph about<|open_end|>
<|open|>data<|:|>ä¦<|close|>IBM Company<|open_end|>
<|open|>req<|:|>Á¼<|close|>Use less than 10 words<|open_end|>
<|open|>req<|:|>¢¬<|close|>Do not use commas<|open_end|>
<|open|>exec<|:|>ÄÐ<|close|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>instruction<|close|>instr<|:|>»ñ<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>input<|close|>data<|:|>ä¦<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>requirement<|close|>req<|:|>Á¼<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>requirement<|close|>req<|:|>¢¬<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>output<|close|>assistant<|:|>ãø<|open_end|>
<|open_end|>
<|open|>assistant<|:|>ãø<|close|>

两字符的块 ID 取自一个固定集合，这个分词器把其中每个 ID 都编码成单个 token，所以无论抽到哪个 ID，指向一个块总是只花两个 token。

角色仍然是一个 user 轮次，但它的成分以五个可单独寻址的块进入模型，由第六个块（exec 块）绑在一起。exec 块说的是：对这份数据执行这条指令，满足这两条要求，把答案写进这里指定的块，也就是模型随后填写的那个 assistant 块。按常规模板，这些成分会被拼成一个字符串，模型得自己推断哪部分是任务、哪部分是对象、哪部分是约束。

提示注入测试：比测试过的最好的前沿模型多挡住 47% 的攻击

间接提示注入是把恶意指令藏在数据载荷里的攻击，载荷可能是检索到的文档、工具返回或用户提供的数据。LLMON 的指令与数据分离针对的正是这个问题。

团队把 LLMON 预览模型和若干开源、闭源模型做了对比，评测基准是 OPI，它把注入放进经典 NLP 任务的数据里，并使用多种攻击策略。报告的指标是稳健性，定义为 1 减去攻击成功率，也就是模型没有执行注入指令的攻击占比。

结果显示，所有非 LLMON 模型都高度易受攻击，执行注入指令的概率很高。在这个基准上 LLMON 基本消除了问题：相对团队测试过的最好的前沿模型多挡住 47% 的攻击，相对最好的开源模型多挡住 95%。团队称在其他基准（ASB 和 StruQ）上观察到类似趋势。

这些基准测的是对静态间接提示注入的稳健性，指令与数据分离直接针对这类攻击。在多轮对话中逐步展开的自适应攻击，团队表示还在改进中。

通用能力与 Granite 4.1 Instruct 持平

团队称安全性的提升没有以通用能力为代价：在各类标准基准上，LLMON 模型与 Granite 4.1 Instruct 模型表现相当。

按团队的说法，如果正在试用 Granite 4.1 3B 或 8B，可以直接换成 LLMON 预览版，通用性能应当相近，而对提示注入的抵抗力强得多。不需要转换流水线，像上面的例子那样给轮次的各部分命名（instruction、data、requirement）就够了，自带的对话模板会把它们转成 LLMON 块。LLMON-converters 库更进一步：如果某个部分本身是结构化的，比如一份 JSON 文档，转换后会保留它的结构，变成带类型、可单独寻址的块，而不是一个不透明的字符串。

训练方法：在后训练阶段学会只认 exec 块

模型从 Granite 4.1 基础检查点出发，而不是从已发布的 Instruct 模型出发，因此 LLMON 行为是在后训练中学到的，没有叠加在现有对话格式之上。

LLMON 定义了六个分隔符，用来标记标签的开始和结束，并支持嵌套和锚定；它们作为保留的单个 token 装进分词器。团队把一份常规指令微调语料重新序列化成 LLMON：每个提示成分变成自己的可寻址块，每个轮次带一个执行块，写明运行哪条指令、作用于哪些输入、输出写到哪里。任务构成与普通 Instruct 模型相同（对话、多轮、RAG、工具调用），团队认为这正是基准表现与常规微调模型接近的原因。

此外，团队在数据里加入诱饵指令和诱饵数据块：它们出现在上下文中，但刻意不被绑定，目标输出保持不变。模型由此学会遵循执行块规定的依赖关系，忽略其余部分。之后是强化学习：五个连续的 GRPO 阶段，涵盖多领域推理、RLHF、知识校准和数学，最后是一个 DPO 阶段，使用一千对在线策略（on-policy）偏好样本，样本来自模型自己对注入尝试的回应。

由此形成的权限规则来自这种布局本身，而不是额外加装的护栏：经由执行块到达的指令具有权威性；作为输入到达的内容（数据、文档、工具模式、工具结果）只是要阅读的材料，不是要执行的命令。执行块没有调用的指令和数据片段会被忽略。团队特别说明，这是一种学到的行为，不是强制保证。 想看它在 LLMON 模型注意力层中的表现，可以试用 Hugging Face Spaces 上的 LLMON Attention Visualization。

自定义词表：以 ScienceWorld 为例

LLMON 不绑定固定模式，可以按自己的领域选标签名和结构，再微调一个适配器来读写它们。团队在 ScienceWorld 上做了演示，这是一个文字类基准，智能体一次发出一条命令完成小学科学任务（比如把水烧开），由模拟器打分。

团队定义了一套描述解题规划轨迹结构的词表，标签包括 instr.task.goal、req.planning_policy.rule、data.state.room、data.state.inventory 和 assistant.next_action。他们用这些标签渲染 ScienceWorld 参考解法的每一步，在 LLMON 模型上微调了一个 LoRA。训练后的模型去玩留出的测试局，并用新词表写出下一步动作。这个 notebook 演示了完整流程，从转换参考轨迹、玩测试局，到把适配器与未训练的基础模型对比打分；面向工具调用智能体的例子在另一个 notebook 里。博客没有给出这个 ScienceWorld 实验的分数。

现在可以怎么试

团队强调这是实验性预览，适合探索和评估，还不适合生产环境。

  • 模型：granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview 和 granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview
  • 可视化演示：LLMON Attention Visualization
  • LLMON 仓库：https://github.com/generative-computing/llmon
  • Mellea：https://github.com/generative-computing/mellea
  • 论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38120、https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.22519

团队欢迎使用者在 GitHub Discussions 里反馈哪些有效、哪些出了问题，以及希望看到哪些用例。做 RAG 或工具调用、担心间接提示注入的团队，可以先在自己的注入样本上对比 LLMON 预览模型和现用模型；同时要记住，已公布的结果覆盖的是静态注入，多轮自适应攻击仍在改进中。

原文

原文由 Hugging Face 博客页面正文转换为 Markdown；正文中的两张图表和一张动图已移到上方媒体区，以 [Image N] 标出原位置；页面标题、作者栏、目录和页面元数据中的封面动图未收录。

LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B

LLMs rely on their context to generate the next set of tokens. Over a long trajectory, the context fills with numerous types of components: a system prompt, past conversation turns, instructions that act on retrieved documents, tool responses or user data, requirements constraining the allowed output, and reasoning chains. The context carries a rich structure, most of which is either implicit to the model or encoded in formats such as JSON that were not designed to be digested by LLMs. This is one of the main reasons LLMs, particularly those on the smaller end of the scale, are brittle and sometimes fail in unexpected ways. The lack of explicit structure can also be exploited by attackers, for example, in the form of prompt injections.

To address this, we developed LLMON (LLM Object Notation, pronounced “lemon”), an LLM-native markup language for explicitly communicating structure and semantics to the models. Semantically coherent components are marked with meaningful tags which are wrapped in reserved special-token delimiters. Data schemas, including nesting, are stated in a way that is unambiguous to a causal LLM. Unique IDs make it possible to point to specific instructions, which could reside anywhere in the context, and bind them to the data payloads they should act on, analogous to the way functions are called and arguments are passed to them in programming languages.

Today we are releasing two experimental preview models, derived from Granite 4.1 base models, trained to consume and generate LLMON-marked text: granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview and granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview. We are also releasing a GitHub repo, which includes a toolkit for working with LLMON and examples of workflows and templates.

What it enables:

  • Indirect prompt injections, hidden in user data, are mostly ignored by LLMON models due to explicit instruction/data separation. For some benchmarks, attack success rates drop to nearly zero, whereas regular instruction-tuned models get hijacked with high probability. This is achieved while maintaining general capability relative to Granite 4.1 Instruct models.
  • Unrelated passages, old chat turns, and tool outputs don’t get pulled into the answer because each instruction is bound to the exact data it applies to.
  • Instructions, data, and requirements are clearly marked so that their structure and meanings at the application’s code level can be leveraged by the model. Try it out in Mellea, which has native LLMON support enabled by automatically LLMONizing its LLM calls.
  • You no longer need to worry about forcing LLMs to observe JSON structure. Use our converters to turn existing JSON into LLMON without loss. You can also define your own structure and associated tags and tune a LoRA on top of the LLMON models to understand it.

Why not JSON?

JSON was designed for parsers, not for causal language models. The tokenizer is not constrained to respect the grammar, and structure is encoded by tokens ({, ", :) that may also appear in normal text. To a model, a quotation mark inside a document and a quotation mark that closes a field are the same token. Escaping rules that are clear to a parser are only statistical patterns to a model. Nesting depth is encoded by counting brackets, which transformers are known to be weak at, especially over long spans.

LLMON, on the other hand, is an XML-like markup whose structural delimiters are reserved special tokens rather than characters, so structure and content use separate parts of the vocabulary. Tags are stated at the beginning of each span, and the boundaries between spans are explicit. Nested structures are stated locally so the model does not need to keep track of the hierarchy over long spans.

Since most teams already have pipelines built around JSON, we created conversion tools and example notebooks that translate JSON to LLMON and back in a lossless manner.

How is LLMON related to chat templates?

LLMON does not replace chat templates; rather, it enriches them. Where regular chat templates tell the model which part belongs to which role (system, user, assistant), LLMON tells it what each component means and how components relate to each other, within and across roles.

The LLMON preview models ship with their own chat template, so you build the same messages list you would pass to any chat model and call apply_chat_template as usual; it renders the LLMON shown below. The only difference is that a turn can now name its parts and mark each one exec: True or False. A part marked True is bound into the exec block at the bottom of the rendered output, which states which instruction to run and what it operates on; a part marked False is still rendered into the context but is referenced by nothing.

messages = [ { "role": "user",
               "instruction": [{ "value": "Write a short paragraph about", "exec": True }],
               "data": [{ "value": "IBM Company", "exec": True }],
               "requirement": [ {"value": "Use less than 10 words", "exec": True},
                                {"value": "Do not use commas", "exec": True}]
             } ]

Which the model receives as the following (with newlines and indentation added here for readability, as the template emits none):

<|open|>instr<|:|>»ñ<|close|>Write a short paragraph about<|open_end|>
<|open|>data<|:|>ä¦<|close|>IBM Company<|open_end|>
<|open|>req<|:|>Á¼<|close|>Use less than 10 words<|open_end|>
<|open|>req<|:|>¢¬<|close|>Do not use commas<|open_end|>
<|open|>exec<|:|>ÄÐ<|close|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>instruction<|close|>instr<|:|>»ñ<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>input<|close|>data<|:|>ä¦<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>requirement<|close|>req<|:|>Á¼<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>requirement<|close|>req<|:|>¢¬<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>output<|close|>assistant<|:|>ãø<|open_end|>
<|open_end|>
<|open|>assistant<|:|>ãø<|close|>

The two-character block IDs are drawn from a fixed set that this tokenizer encodes as single tokens, so addressing a block always costs two tokens regardless of which ID is drawn.

The role is still a single user turn, but its components reach the model as five separate addressable blocks, bound together by a sixth (the exec block) that states: run this instruction, on this data, subject to these two requirements, and put the answer in the block named here, which is the same assistant block the model then fills. A conventional template would have flattened all components into one string and left the model to infer which part was the task, which was the subject, and which were constraints.

How LLMON addresses prompt injection attacks

Indirect prompt injection is a type of attack where a malicious instruction is hidden in a data payload, such as a retrieved document, a tool response, or user-provided data. This is the problem LLMON’s instruction/data separation is designed to address.

We compared the LLMON previews against several open-source and closed-source models. We evaluated on the OPI benchmark, which places the injection in the data of classic NLP tasks. Several attack strategies are employed. We report robustness, defined as 1 − attack success rate: the share of attacks where the model does not carry out the injected instruction.

[Image 1: OPI]

All non-LLMON models are highly susceptible, carrying out the injected instructions with high probability. LLMON practically eliminates the problem on this benchmark, avoiding 47% more attacks relative to the best frontier model that we tested, and 95% more than the best open-source model. We observe similar trends on other benchmarks (ASB and StruQ). It is worth noting that these benchmarks test robustness to static indirect prompt injections. The instruction/data separation directly addresses this type of attack. We are actively working on also improving adaptive attacks which unfold over many chat turns.

General capability

Safety gains don’t come at the expense of general capability. Across standard benchmark categories, the LLMON models perform on par with the Granite 4.1 Instruct models.

[Image 2: Granite-4.1 vs LLMON]

In short, if you’re experimenting with Granite 4.1 3B or 8B today, you can swap in the LLMON preview and should see comparable general performance with much stronger resistance to prompt injection. No conversion pipeline is required. Naming the turn's parts (e.g., instruction, data, requirement as in the example above) is enough. The shipped chat template turns those into LLMON blocks for you. Our LLMON-converters library goes one level deeper: if a part is itself structured, such as a JSON document, LLMONizing it preserves that structure as typed, individually addressable blocks, instead of one opaque string.

How we trained the models

The models start from Granite 4.1 base checkpoints rather than the released instruct models, so LLMON behavior is learned during post-training rather than layered on an existing chat format.

LLMON defines six delimiters that mark the start and end of tags and allow nesting and anchoring; they are installed in the tokenizer as reserved single tokens. We re-serialized a conventional instruction-tuning corpus into LLMON: every prompt component becomes its own addressable block, and each turn carries an execution block naming which instruction to run, which inputs it operates on, and where the output goes. The task mix is the one a normal instruct model sees (chat, multi-turn, RAG, tool calling), which is why benchmark performance stays close to the conventionally tuned model. In addition, we augment the data with decoy instructions and data blocks that are present in context but deliberately left unbound, while the target output is unchanged. So the model learns to follow the dependencies dictated by the execution block and ignore the rest. Reinforcement learning follows: five sequential GRPO stages spanning multi-domain reasoning, RLHF, knowledge calibration, and math, followed by a final DPO stage on a thousand on-policy preference pairs built from the model’s own responses to injection attempts.

The resulting privilege rule falls out of this layout rather than an added guardrail: an instruction reached through an execution block is authoritative, while anything reached as input (data, documents, tool schemas, tool results) is material to read, not a command to follow. Furthermore, instructions and data spans that are not called on in the execution block are ignored. This is a learned behavior, not an enforced guarantee. To see how this plays out in the attention layers of a LLMON model, try the LLMON Attention Visualization on Hugging Face Spaces.

[Image 3: Attention Demo]

Bring your own vocabulary (ScienceWorld)

LLMON is not tied to a fixed schema: you can choose tag names and structure that fit your domain and fine-tune an adapter to read and write them. We demonstrate this on ScienceWorld, a text-based benchmark where an agent carries out elementary science tasks (such as boiling water) by issuing one command at a time and receiving a score from the simulator. We defined a vocabulary capturing the structure in the planning trajectories involved in solving these tasks. The vocabulary includes tags such as instr.task.goal, req.planning_policy.rule, data.state.room, data.state.inventory and assistant.next_action. We rendered every step of ScienceWorld's reference solutions with these tags and tuned a LoRA on top of a LLMON model. The trained model then plays held-out games and writes its next action in the new vocabulary. This notebook walks through the full workflow, from converting reference trajectories to playing the test games and scoring the adapter against the untrained base model. Another example for tool-calling agents can be found in this notebook.

Try it today

This is an experimental preview, ready for exploration and evaluation but not for production.

  • Models: granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview & granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview
  • Visualization Demo: LLMON Attention Visualization
  • LLMON Repo: https://github.com/generative-computing/llmon
  • Mellea: https://github.com/generative-computing/mellea
  • Papers: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38120, https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.22519

Tell us what you find: what worked, what broke, and which use cases you’d like to see. Post it in GitHub Discussions.
