相关链接：https://github.com/generative-computing/llmon
item.content:encoded:
IBM Granite 团队推出面向大模型的标记语言 LLMON 和两个 Granite 4.1 预览模型：结构分隔符改用保留 token，exec 块绑定指令与数据；团队称在 OPI 基准上比所测最好的前沿模型多挡住 47% 的注入攻击，通用能力与 Instruct 版持平，仍是实验性预览。

中文改写

大语言模型靠上下文生成下一批 token。在一段很长的交互里，上下文会塞满各种成分：系统提示、过去的对话轮次、作用于检索文档的指令、工具返回或用户数据、限制输出的要求，以及推理链。IBM Granite 团队在 Hugging Face 博客上指出，这些成分本来有丰富的结构，但大多要么只是隐含在模型里，要么用 JSON 这类并非为大模型设计的格式表达。团队认为，这是大模型（尤其是较小的模型）脆弱、会以意想不到的方式出错的主要原因之一；结构不明确也会被攻击者利用，比如提示注入。

为此，团队开发了 LLMON（LLM Object Notation，读作 “lemon”），一种面向大模型的原生标记语言，用来把结构和语义明确地告诉模型。语义上连贯的成分用有意义的标签标记，标签外面包着保留的特殊 token 分隔符。数据模式（包括嵌套）以因果语言模型不会误解的方式写明。每个块有唯一 ID，可以指向上下文中任意位置的某条指令，并把它绑定到该指令要处理的数据上，类似编程语言里调用函数并传入参数。

团队同时发布了两个基于 Granite 4.1 基础模型、经训练可以读写 LLMON 标记文本的实验性预览模型：granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview 和 granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview，以及一个 GitHub 仓库，内含处理 LLMON 的工具包和工作流、模板示例。

团队给出的四项用途

  • 抵御间接提示注入。 藏在用户数据里的注入指令，大多会被 LLMON 模型忽略，因为指令和数据是明确分开的。在部分基准上攻击成功率降到接近零，而常规指令微调模型被劫持的概率很高。团队称这是在保持与 Granite 4.1 Instruct 模型相当的通用能力的前提下做到的。
  • 不串味。 每条指令都绑定到它要处理的确切数据，无关段落、旧的对话轮次和工具输出不会被拉进答案。
  • 应用代码里的结构可以被模型利用。 指令、数据和要求都有清楚的标记。可以在 Mellea 里试用，它会自动把大模型调用转成 LLMON，原生支持这种格式。
  • 不用再逼模型遵守 JSON 结构。 团队提供的转换器可以把现有 JSON 无损转成 LLMON；也可以自定义结构和标签，在 LLMON 模型上微调一个 LoRA 来理解它们。

为什么不用 JSON

JSON 是为解析器设计的，不是为因果语言模型设计的。分词器不受语法约束，而结构是靠 {、"、: 这些在普通文本里也会出现的 token 表达的。在模型眼里，文档里的一个引号和结束一个字段的引号是同一个 token。解析器眼中清清楚楚的转义规则，在模型那里只是统计规律。嵌套深度靠数括号来体现，而 Transformer 在这方面已知较弱，跨度越长越明显。

LLMON 是一种类 XML 的标记，它的结构分隔符是保留的特殊 token 而不是字符，因此结构和内容使用词表中互不重叠的部分。标签写在每个片段的开头，片段之间的边界是明确的。嵌套结构在局部写明，模型不必在长跨度上记住层级关系。

考虑到多数团队已有基于 JSON 的流水线，团队提供了转换工具和示例 notebook，可以在 JSON 和 LLMON 之间无损互转。

与对话模板的关系：在角色之外再标出“每一块是什么”

LLMON 不替代对话模板（chat template），它在对话模板之上补充信息。常规对话模板告诉模型哪部分属于哪个角色（system、user、assistant）；LLMON 还告诉模型每个成分是什么意思，以及成分之间在角色内、跨角色的关系。

预览模型自带对话模板，开发者照常构造传给任何对话模型的 messages 列表，再照常调用 apply_chat_template。唯一的区别是，一个轮次可以给自己的各部分命名，并把每部分标为 exec: True 或 False。标为 True 的部分会被绑定进渲染结果底部的 exec 块，这个块写明要执行哪条指令、作用于什么；标为 False 的部分仍会渲染进上下文，但没有任何地方引用它。博客给出的例子是：

messages = [ { "role": "user",
               "instruction": [{ "value": "Write a short paragraph about", "exec": True }],
               "data": [{ "value": "IBM Company", "exec": True }],
               "requirement": [ {"value": "Use less than 10 words", "exec": True},
                                {"value": "Do not use commas", "exec": True}]
             } ]

模型实际收到的是下面这段（为便于阅读加了换行和缩进，模板本身不输出这些）：

<|open|>instr<|:|>»ñ<|close|>Write a short paragraph about<|open_end|>
<|open|>data<|:|>ä¦<|close|>IBM Company<|open_end|>
<|open|>req<|:|>Á¼<|close|>Use less than 10 words<|open_end|>
<|open|>req<|:|>¢¬<|close|>Do not use commas<|open_end|>
<|open|>exec<|:|>ÄÐ<|close|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>instruction<|close|>instr<|:|>»ñ<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>input<|close|>data<|:|>ä¦<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>requirement<|close|>req<|:|>Á¼<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>requirement<|close|>req<|:|>¢¬<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>output<|close|>assistant<|:|>ãø<|open_end|>
<|open_end|>
<|open|>assistant<|:|>ãø<|close|>

两字符的块 ID 取自一个固定集合，这个分词器把其中每个 ID 都编码成单个 token，所以无论抽到哪个 ID，指向一个块总是只花两个 token。

角色仍然是一个 user 轮次，但它的成分以五个可单独寻址的块进入模型，由第六个块（exec 块）绑在一起。exec 块说的是：对这份数据执行这条指令，满足这两条要求，把答案写进这里指定的块，也就是模型随后填写的那个 assistant 块。按常规模板，这些成分会被拼成一个字符串，模型得自己推断哪部分是任务、哪部分是对象、哪部分是约束。

提示注入测试：比测试过的最好的前沿模型多挡住 47% 的攻击

间接提示注入是把恶意指令藏在数据载荷里的攻击，载荷可能是检索到的文档、工具返回或用户提供的数据。LLMON 的指令与数据分离针对的正是这个问题。

团队把 LLMON 预览模型和若干开源、闭源模型做了对比，评测基准是 OPI，它把注入放进经典 NLP 任务的数据里，并使用多种攻击策略。报告的指标是稳健性，定义为 1 减去攻击成功率，也就是模型没有执行注入指令的攻击占比。

结果显示，所有非 LLMON 模型都高度易受攻击，执行注入指令的概率很高。在这个基准上 LLMON 基本消除了问题：相对团队测试过的最好的前沿模型多挡住 47% 的攻击，相对最好的开源模型多挡住 95%。团队称在其他基准（ASB 和 StruQ）上观察到类似趋势。

这些基准测的是对静态间接提示注入的稳健性，指令与数据分离直接针对这类攻击。在多轮对话中逐步展开的自适应攻击，团队表示还在改进中。

通用能力与 Granite 4.1 Instruct 持平

团队称安全性的提升没有以通用能力为代价：在各类标准基准上，LLMON 模型与 Granite 4.1 Instruct 模型表现相当。

按团队的说法，如果正在试用 Granite 4.1 3B 或 8B，可以直接换成 LLMON 预览版，通用性能应当相近，而对提示注入的抵抗力强得多。不需要转换流水线，像上面的例子那样给轮次的各部分命名（instruction、data、requirement）就够了，自带的对话模板会把它们转成 LLMON 块。LLMON-converters 库更进一步：如果某个部分本身是结构化的，比如一份 JSON 文档，转换后会保留它的结构，变成带类型、可单独寻址的块，而不是一个不透明的字符串。

训练方法：在后训练阶段学会只认 exec 块

模型从 Granite 4.1 基础检查点出发，而不是从已发布的 Instruct 模型出发，因此 LLMON 行为是在后训练中学到的，没有叠加在现有对话格式之上。

LLMON 定义了六个分隔符，用来标记标签的开始和结束，并支持嵌套和锚定；它们作为保留的单个 token 装进分词器。团队把一份常规指令微调语料重新序列化成 LLMON：每个提示成分变成自己的可寻址块，每个轮次带一个执行块，写明运行哪条指令、作用于哪些输入、输出写到哪里。任务构成与普通 Instruct 模型相同（对话、多轮、RAG、工具调用），团队认为这正是基准表现与常规微调模型接近的原因。

此外，团队在数据里加入诱饵指令和诱饵数据块：它们出现在上下文中，但刻意不被绑定，目标输出保持不变。模型由此学会遵循执行块规定的依赖关系，忽略其余部分。之后是强化学习：五个连续的 GRPO 阶段，涵盖多领域推理、RLHF、知识校准和数学，最后是一个 DPO 阶段，使用一千对在线策略（on-policy）偏好样本，样本来自模型自己对注入尝试的回应。

由此形成的权限规则来自这种布局本身，而不是额外加装的护栏：经由执行块到达的指令具有权威性；作为输入到达的内容（数据、文档、工具模式、工具结果）只是要阅读的材料，不是要执行的命令。执行块没有调用的指令和数据片段会被忽略。团队特别说明，这是一种学到的行为，不是强制保证。 想看它在 LLMON 模型注意力层中的表现，可以试用 Hugging Face Spaces 上的 LLMON Attention Visualization。

自定义词表：以 ScienceWorld 为例

LLMON 不绑定固定模式，可以按自己的领域选标签名和结构，再微调一个适配器来读写它们。团队在 ScienceWorld 上做了演示，这是一个文字类基准，智能体一次发出一条命令完成小学科学任务（比如把水烧开），由模拟器打分。

团队定义了一套描述解题规划轨迹结构的词表，标签包括 instr.task.goal、req.planning_policy.rule、data.state.room、data.state.inventory 和 assistant.next_action。他们用这些标签渲染 ScienceWorld 参考解法的每一步，在 LLMON 模型上微调了一个 LoRA。训练后的模型去玩留出的测试局，并用新词表写出下一步动作。这个 notebook 演示了完整流程，从转换参考轨迹、玩测试局，到把适配器与未训练的基础模型对比打分；面向工具调用智能体的例子在另一个 notebook 里。博客没有给出这个 ScienceWorld 实验的分数。

现在可以怎么试

团队强调这是实验性预览，适合探索和评估，还不适合生产环境。

  • 模型：granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview 和 granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview
  • 可视化演示：LLMON Attention Visualization
  • LLMON 仓库：https://github.com/generative-computing/llmon
  • Mellea：https://github.com/generative-computing/mellea
  • 论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38120、https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.22519

团队欢迎使用者在 GitHub Discussions 里反馈哪些有效、哪些出了问题，以及希望看到哪些用例。做 RAG 或工具调用、担心间接提示注入的团队，可以先在自己的注入样本上对比 LLMON 预览模型和现用模型；同时要记住，已公布的结果覆盖的是静态注入，多轮自适应攻击仍在改进中。

原文

原文由 Hugging Face 博客页面正文转换为 Markdown；正文中的两张图表和一张动图已移到上方媒体区，以 [Image N] 标出原位置；页面标题、作者栏、目录和页面元数据中的封面动图未收录。

LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B

LLMs rely on their context to generate the next set of tokens. Over a long trajectory, the context fills with numerous types of components: a system prompt, past conversation turns, instructions that act on retrieved documents, tool responses or user data, requirements constraining the allowed output, and reasoning chains. The context carries a rich structure, most of which is either implicit to the model or encoded in formats such as JSON that were not designed to be digested by LLMs. This is one of the main reasons LLMs, particularly those on the smaller end of the scale, are brittle and sometimes fail in unexpected ways. The lack of explicit structure can also be exploited by attackers, for example, in the form of prompt injections.

To address this, we developed LLMON (LLM Object Notation, pronounced “lemon”), an LLM-native markup language for explicitly communicating structure and semantics to the models. Semantically coherent components are marked with meaningful tags which are wrapped in reserved special-token delimiters. Data schemas, including nesting, are stated in a way that is unambiguous to a causal LLM. Unique IDs make it possible to point to specific instructions, which could reside anywhere in the context, and bind them to the data payloads they should act on, analogous to the way functions are called and arguments are passed to them in programming languages.

Today we are releasing two experimental preview models, derived from Granite 4.1 base models, trained to consume and generate LLMON-marked text: granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview and granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview. We are also releasing a GitHub repo, which includes a toolkit for working with LLMON and examples of workflows and templates.

What it enables:

  • Indirect prompt injections, hidden in user data, are mostly ignored by LLMON models due to explicit instruction/data separation. For some benchmarks, attack success rates drop to nearly zero, whereas regular instruction-tuned models get hijacked with high probability. This is achieved while maintaining general capability relative to Granite 4.1 Instruct models.
  • Unrelated passages, old chat turns, and tool outputs don’t get pulled into the answer because each instruction is bound to the exact data it applies to.
  • Instructions, data, and requirements are clearly marked so that their structure and meanings at the application’s code level can be leveraged by the model. Try it out in Mellea, which has native LLMON support enabled by automatically LLMONizing its LLM calls.
  • You no longer need to worry about forcing LLMs to observe JSON structure. Use our converters to turn existing JSON into LLMON without loss. You can also define your own structure and associated tags and tune a LoRA on top of the LLMON models to understand it.

Why not JSON?

JSON was designed for parsers, not for causal language models. The tokenizer is not constrained to respect the grammar, and structure is encoded by tokens ({, ", :) that may also appear in normal text. To a model, a quotation mark inside a document and a quotation mark that closes a field are the same token. Escaping rules that are clear to a parser are only statistical patterns to a model. Nesting depth is encoded by counting brackets, which transformers are known to be weak at, especially over long spans.

LLMON, on the other hand, is an XML-like markup whose structural delimiters are reserved special tokens rather than characters, so structure and content use separate parts of the vocabulary. Tags are stated at the beginning of each span, and the boundaries between spans are explicit. Nested structures are stated locally so the model does not need to keep track of the hierarchy over long spans.

Since most teams already have pipelines built around JSON, we created conversion tools and example notebooks that translate JSON to LLMON and back in a lossless manner.

How is LLMON related to chat templates?

LLMON does not replace chat templates; rather, it enriches them. Where regular chat templates tell the model which part belongs to which role (system, user, assistant), LLMON tells it what each component means and how components relate to each other, within and across roles.

The LLMON preview models ship with their own chat template, so you build the same messages list you would pass to any chat model and call apply_chat_template as usual; it renders the LLMON shown below. The only difference is that a turn can now name its parts and mark each one exec: True or False. A part marked True is bound into the exec block at the bottom of the rendered output, which states which instruction to run and what it operates on; a part marked False is still rendered into the context but is referenced by nothing.

messages = [ { "role": "user",
               "instruction": [{ "value": "Write a short paragraph about", "exec": True }],
               "data": [{ "value": "IBM Company", "exec": True }],
               "requirement": [ {"value": "Use less than 10 words", "exec": True},
                                {"value": "Do not use commas", "exec": True}]
             } ]

Which the model receives as the following (with newlines and indentation added here for readability, as the template emits none):

<|open|>instr<|:|>»ñ<|close|>Write a short paragraph about<|open_end|>
<|open|>data<|:|>ä¦<|close|>IBM Company<|open_end|>
<|open|>req<|:|>Á¼<|close|>Use less than 10 words<|open_end|>
<|open|>req<|:|>¢¬<|close|>Do not use commas<|open_end|>
<|open|>exec<|:|>ÄÐ<|close|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>instruction<|close|>instr<|:|>»ñ<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>input<|close|>data<|:|>ä¦<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>requirement<|close|>req<|:|>Á¼<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>requirement<|close|>req<|:|>¢¬<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>output<|close|>assistant<|:|>ãø<|open_end|>
<|open_end|>
<|open|>assistant<|:|>ãø<|close|>

The two-character block IDs are drawn from a fixed set that this tokenizer encodes as single tokens, so addressing a block always costs two tokens regardless of which ID is drawn.

The role is still a single user turn, but its components reach the model as five separate addressable blocks, bound together by a sixth (the exec block) that states: run this instruction, on this data, subject to these two requirements, and put the answer in the block named here, which is the same assistant block the model then fills. A conventional template would have flattened all components into one string and left the model to infer which part was the task, which was the subject, and which were constraints.

How LLMON addresses prompt injection attacks

Indirect prompt injection is a type of attack where a malicious instruction is hidden in a data payload, such as a retrieved document, a tool response, or user-provided data. This is the problem LLMON’s instruction/data separation is designed to address.

We compared the LLMON previews against several open-source and closed-source models. We evaluated on the OPI benchmark, which places the injection in the data of classic NLP tasks. Several attack strategies are employed. We report robustness, defined as 1 − attack success rate: the share of attacks where the model does not carry out the injected instruction.

[Image 1: OPI]

All non-LLMON models are highly susceptible, carrying out the injected instructions with high probability. LLMON practically eliminates the problem on this benchmark, avoiding 47% more attacks relative to the best frontier model that we tested, and 95% more than the best open-source model. We observe similar trends on other benchmarks (ASB and StruQ). It is worth noting that these benchmarks test robustness to static indirect prompt injections. The instruction/data separation directly addresses this type of attack. We are actively working on also improving adaptive attacks which unfold over many chat turns.

General capability

Safety gains don’t come at the expense of general capability. Across standard benchmark categories, the LLMON models perform on par with the Granite 4.1 Instruct models.

[Image 2: Granite-4.1 vs LLMON]

In short, if you’re experimenting with Granite 4.1 3B or 8B today, you can swap in the LLMON preview and should see comparable general performance with much stronger resistance to prompt injection. No conversion pipeline is required. Naming the turn's parts (e.g., instruction, data, requirement as in the example above) is enough. The shipped chat template turns those into LLMON blocks for you. Our LLMON-converters library goes one level deeper: if a part is itself structured, such as a JSON document, LLMONizing it preserves that structure as typed, individually addressable blocks, instead of one opaque string.

How we trained the models

The models start from Granite 4.1 base checkpoints rather than the released instruct models, so LLMON behavior is learned during post-training rather than layered on an existing chat format.

LLMON defines six delimiters that mark the start and end of tags and allow nesting and anchoring; they are installed in the tokenizer as reserved single tokens. We re-serialized a conventional instruction-tuning corpus into LLMON: every prompt component becomes its own addressable block, and each turn carries an execution block naming which instruction to run, which inputs it operates on, and where the output goes. The task mix is the one a normal instruct model sees (chat, multi-turn, RAG, tool calling), which is why benchmark performance stays close to the conventionally tuned model. In addition, we augment the data with decoy instructions and data blocks that are present in context but deliberately left unbound, while the target output is unchanged. So the model learns to follow the dependencies dictated by the execution block and ignore the rest. Reinforcement learning follows: five sequential GRPO stages spanning multi-domain reasoning, RLHF, knowledge calibration, and math, followed by a final DPO stage on a thousand on-policy preference pairs built from the model’s own responses to injection attempts.

The resulting privilege rule falls out of this layout rather than an added guardrail: an instruction reached through an execution block is authoritative, while anything reached as input (data, documents, tool schemas, tool results) is material to read, not a command to follow. Furthermore, instructions and data spans that are not called on in the execution block are ignored. This is a learned behavior, not an enforced guarantee. To see how this plays out in the attention layers of a LLMON model, try the LLMON Attention Visualization on Hugging Face Spaces.

[Image 3: Attention Demo]

Bring your own vocabulary (ScienceWorld)

LLMON is not tied to a fixed schema: you can choose tag names and structure that fit your domain and fine-tune an adapter to read and write them. We demonstrate this on ScienceWorld, a text-based benchmark where an agent carries out elementary science tasks (such as boiling water) by issuing one command at a time and receiving a score from the simulator. We defined a vocabulary capturing the structure in the planning trajectories involved in solving these tasks. The vocabulary includes tags such as instr.task.goal, req.planning_policy.rule, data.state.room, data.state.inventory and assistant.next_action. We rendered every step of ScienceWorld's reference solutions with these tags and tuned a LoRA on top of a LLMON model. The trained model then plays held-out games and writes its next action in the new vocabulary. This notebook walks through the full workflow, from converting reference trajectories to playing the test games and scoring the adapter against the untrained base model. Another example for tool-calling agents can be found in this notebook.

Try it today

This is an experimental preview, ready for exploration and evaluation but not for production.

  • Visualization Demo: LLMON Attention Visualization
  • LLMON Repo: https://github.com/generative-computing/llmon
  • Mellea: https://github.com/generative-computing/mellea

LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B

原文由 Hugging Face 博客页面正文转换为 Markdown；正文中的两张图表和一张动图已移到上方媒体区，以 [Image N] 标出原位置；页面标题、作者栏、目录和页面元数据中的封面动图未收录。

LLMs rely on their context to generate the next set of tokens. Over a long trajectory, the context fills with numerous types of components: a system prompt, past conversation turns, instructions that act on retrieved documents, tool responses or user data, requirements constraining the allowed output, and reasoning chains. The context carries a rich structure, most of which is either implicit to the model or encoded in formats such as JSON that were not designed to be digested by LLMs. This is one of the main reasons LLMs, particularly those on the smaller end of the scale, are brittle and sometimes fail in unexpected ways. The lack of explicit structure can also be exploited by attackers, for example, in the form of prompt injections.

To address this, we developed LLMON (LLM Object Notation, pronounced “lemon”), an LLM-native markup language for explicitly communicating structure and semantics to the models. Semantically coherent components are marked with meaningful tags which are wrapped in reserved special-token delimiters. Data schemas, including nesting, are stated in a way that is unambiguous to a causal LLM. Unique IDs make it possible to point to specific instructions, which could reside anywhere in the context, and bind them to the data payloads they should act on, analogous to the way functions are called and arguments are passed to them in programming languages.

Today we are releasing two experimental preview models, derived from Granite 4.1 base models, trained to consume and generate LLMON-marked text: granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview and granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview. We are also releasing a GitHub repo, which includes a toolkit for working with LLMON and examples of workflows and templates.

What it enables:

  • Indirect prompt injections, hidden in user data, are mostly ignored by LLMON models due to explicit instruction/data separation. For some benchmarks, attack success rates drop to nearly zero, whereas regular instruction-tuned models get hijacked with high probability. This is achieved while maintaining general capability relative to Granite 4.1 Instruct models.
  • Unrelated passages, old chat turns, and tool outputs don’t get pulled into the answer because each instruction is bound to the exact data it applies to.
  • Instructions, data, and requirements are clearly marked so that their structure and meanings at the application’s code level can be leveraged by the model. Try it out in Mellea, which has native LLMON support enabled by automatically LLMONizing its LLM calls.
  • You no longer need to worry about forcing LLMs to observe JSON structure. Use our converters to turn existing JSON into LLMON without loss. You can also define your own structure and associated tags and tune a LoRA on top of the LLMON models to understand it.

Why not JSON?

JSON was designed for parsers, not for causal language models. The tokenizer is not constrained to respect the grammar, and structure is encoded by tokens ({, ", :) that may also appear in normal text. To a model, a quotation mark inside a document and a quotation mark that closes a field are the same token. Escaping rules that are clear to a parser are only statistical patterns to a model. Nesting depth is encoded by counting brackets, which transformers are known to be weak at, especially over long spans.

LLMON, on the other hand, is an XML-like markup whose structural delimiters are reserved special tokens rather than characters, so structure and content use separate parts of the vocabulary. Tags are stated at the beginning of each span, and the boundaries between spans are explicit. Nested structures are stated locally so the model does not need to keep track of the hierarchy over long spans.

Since most teams already have pipelines built around JSON, we created conversion tools and example notebooks that translate JSON to LLMON and back in a lossless manner.

How is LLMON related to chat templates?

LLMON does not replace chat templates; rather, it enriches them. Where regular chat templates tell the model which part belongs to which role (system, user, assistant), LLMON tells it what each component means and how components relate to each other, within and across roles.

The LLMON preview models ship with their own chat template, so you build the same messages list you would pass to any chat model and call apply_chat_template as usual; it renders the LLMON shown below. The only difference is that a turn can now name its parts and mark each one exec: True or False. A part marked True is bound into the exec block at the bottom of the rendered output, which states which instruction to run and what it operates on; a part marked False is still rendered into the context but is referenced by nothing.

messages = [ { "role": "user",
               "instruction": [{ "value": "Write a short paragraph about", "exec": True }],
               "data": [{ "value": "IBM Company", "exec": True }],
               "requirement": [ {"value": "Use less than 10 words", "exec": True},
                                {"value": "Do not use commas", "exec": True}]
             } ]

Which the model receives as the following (with newlines and indentation added here for readability, as the template emits none):

<|open|>instr<|:|>»ñ<|close|>Write a short paragraph about<|open_end|>
<|open|>data<|:|>ä¦<|close|>IBM Company<|open_end|>
<|open|>req<|:|>Á¼<|close|>Use less than 10 words<|open_end|>
<|open|>req<|:|>¢¬<|close|>Do not use commas<|open_end|>
<|open|>exec<|:|>ÄÐ<|close|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>instruction<|close|>instr<|:|>»ñ<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>input<|close|>data<|:|>ä¦<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>requirement<|close|>req<|:|>Á¼<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>requirement<|close|>req<|:|>¢¬<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>output<|close|>assistant<|:|>ãø<|open_end|>
<|open_end|>
<|open|>assistant<|:|>ãø<|close|>

The two-character block IDs are drawn from a fixed set that this tokenizer encodes as single tokens, so addressing a block always costs two tokens regardless of which ID is drawn.

The role is still a single user turn, but its components reach the model as five separate addressable blocks, bound together by a sixth (the exec block) that states: run this instruction, on this data, subject to these two requirements, and put the answer in the block named here, which is the same assistant block the model then fills. A conventional template would have flattened all components into one string and left the model to infer which part was the task, which was the subject, and which were constraints.

How LLMON addresses prompt injection attacks

Indirect prompt injection is a type of attack where a malicious instruction is hidden in a data payload, such as a retrieved document, a tool response, or user-provided data. This is the problem LLMON’s instruction/data separation is designed to address.

We compared the LLMON previews against several open-source and closed-source models. We evaluated on the OPI benchmark, which places the injection in the data of classic NLP tasks. Several attack strategies are employed. We report robustness, defined as 1 − attack success rate: the share of attacks where the model does not carry out the injected instruction.

[Image 1: OPI]

All non-LLMON models are highly susceptible, carrying out the injected instructions with high probability. LLMON practically eliminates the problem on this benchmark, avoiding 47% more attacks relative to the best frontier model that we tested, and 95% more than the best open-source model. We observe similar trends on other benchmarks (ASB and StruQ). It is worth noting that these benchmarks test robustness to static indirect prompt injections. The instruction/data separation directly addresses this type of attack. We are actively working on also improving adaptive attacks which unfold over many chat turns.

General capability

Safety gains don’t come at the expense of general capability. Across standard benchmark categories, the LLMON models perform on par with the Granite 4.1 Instruct models.

[Image 2: Granite-4.1 vs LLMON]

In short, if you’re experimenting with Granite 4.1 3B or 8B today, you can swap in the LLMON preview and should see comparable general performance with much stronger resistance to prompt injection. No conversion pipeline is required. Naming the turn's parts (e.g., instruction, data, requirement as in the example above) is enough. The shipped chat template turns those into LLMON blocks for you. Our LLMON-converters library goes one level deeper: if a part is itself structured, such as a JSON document, LLMONizing it preserves that structure as typed, individually addressable blocks, instead of one opaque string.

How we trained the models

The models start from Granite 4.1 base checkpoints rather than the released instruct models, so LLMON behavior is learned during post-training rather than layered on an existing chat format.

LLMON defines six delimiters that mark the start and end of tags and allow nesting and anchoring; they are installed in the tokenizer as reserved single tokens. We re-serialized a conventional instruction-tuning corpus into LLMON: every prompt component becomes its own addressable block, and each turn carries an execution block naming which instruction to run, which inputs it operates on, and where the output goes. The task mix is the one a normal instruct model sees (chat, multi-turn, RAG, tool calling), which is why benchmark performance stays close to the conventionally tuned model. In addition, we augment the data with decoy instructions and data blocks that are present in context but deliberately left unbound, while the target output is unchanged. So the model learns to follow the dependencies dictated by the execution block and ignore the rest. Reinforcement learning follows: five sequential GRPO stages spanning multi-domain reasoning, RLHF, knowledge calibration, and math, followed by a final DPO stage on a thousand on-policy preference pairs built from the model’s own responses to injection attempts.

The resulting privilege rule falls out of this layout rather than an added guardrail: an instruction reached through an execution block is authoritative, while anything reached as input (data, documents, tool schemas, tool results) is material to read, not a command to follow. Furthermore, instructions and data spans that are not called on in the execution block are ignored. This is a learned behavior, not an enforced guarantee. To see how this plays out in the attention layers of a LLMON model, try the LLMON Attention Visualization on Hugging Face Spaces.

[Image 3: Attention Demo]

Bring your own vocabulary (ScienceWorld)

LLMON is not tied to a fixed schema: you can choose tag names and structure that fit your domain and fine-tune an adapter to read and write them. We demonstrate this on ScienceWorld, a text-based benchmark where an agent carries out elementary science tasks (such as boiling water) by issuing one command at a time and receiving a score from the simulator. We defined a vocabulary capturing the structure in the planning trajectories involved in solving these tasks. The vocabulary includes tags such as instr.task.goal, req.planning_policy.rule, data.state.room, data.state.inventory and assistant.next_action. We rendered every step of ScienceWorld's reference solutions with these tags and tuned a LoRA on top of a LLMON model. The trained model then plays held-out games and writes its next action in the new vocabulary. This notebook walks through the full workflow, from converting reference trajectories to playing the test games and scoring the adapter against the untrained base model. Another example for tool-calling agents can be found in this notebook.

Try it today

This is an experimental preview, ready for exploration and evaluation but not for production.

  • Models: granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview & granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview
  • Visualization Demo: LLMON Attention Visualization

Tell us what you find: what worked, what broke, and which use cases you’d like to see. Post it in GitHub Discussions.

"}, "rewrite": {"title": "IBM 发布 LLMON：用特殊 token 把指令和数据分开，Granite 4.1 预览模型抵御提示注入", "markdown": "大语言模型靠上下文生成下一批 token。在一段很长的交互里，上下文会塞满各种成分：系统提示、过去的对话轮次、作用于检索文档的指令、工具返回或用户数据、限制输出的要求，以及推理链。IBM Granite 团队在 Hugging Face 博客上指出，这些成分本来有丰富的结构，但大多要么只是隐含在模型里，要么用 JSON 这类并非为大模型设计的格式表达。团队认为，这是大模型（尤其是较小的模型）脆弱、会以意想不到的方式出错的主要原因之一；结构不明确也会被攻击者利用，比如提示注入。 为此，团队开发了 **LLMON**（LLM Object Notation，读作 “lemon”），一种面向大模型的原生标记语言，用来把结构和语义明确地告诉模型。语义上连贯的成分用有意义的标签标记，标签外面包着保留的特殊 token 分隔符。数据模式（包括嵌套）以因果语言模型不会误解的方式写明。每个块有唯一 ID，可以指向上下文中任意位置的某条指令，并把它绑定到该指令要处理的数据上，类似编程语言里调用函数并传入参数。 团队同时发布了两个基于 Granite 4.1 基础模型、经训练可以读写 LLMON 标记文本的实验性预览模型：[granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview](https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-4.1-3b-llmon-preview) 和 [granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview](https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-4.1-8b-llmon-preview)，以及一个 [GitHub 仓库](https://github.com/generative-computing/llmon)，内含处理 LLMON 的工具包和工作流、模板示例。 ## 团队给出的四项用途 - **抵御间接提示注入。** 藏在用户数据里的注入指令，大多会被 LLMON 模型忽略，因为指令和数据是明确分开的。在部分基准上攻击成功率降到接近零，而常规指令微调模型被劫持的概率很高。团队称这是在保持与 Granite 4.1 Instruct 模型相当的通用能力的前提下做到的。 - **不串味。** 每条指令都绑定到它要处理的确切数据，无关段落、旧的对话轮次和工具输出不会被拉进答案。 - **应用代码里的结构可以被模型利用。** 指令、数据和要求都有清楚的标记。可以在 [Mellea](https://github.com/generative-computing/mellea) 里试用，它会自动把大模型调用转成 LLMON，原生支持这种格式。 - **不用再逼模型遵守 JSON 结构。** 团队提供的转换器可以把现有 JSON 无损转成 LLMON；也可以自定义结构和标签，在 LLMON 模型上微调一个 LoRA 来理解它们。 ## 为什么不用 JSON JSON 是为解析器设计的，不是为因果语言模型设计的。分词器不受语法约束，而结构是靠 `{`、`"`、`:` 这些在普通文本里也会出现的 token 表达的。在模型眼里，文档里的一个引号和结束一个字段的引号是同一个 token。解析器眼中清清楚楚的转义规则，在模型那里只是统计规律。嵌套深度靠数括号来体现，而 Transformer 在这方面已知较弱，跨度越长越明显。 LLMON 是一种类 XML 的标记，它的结构分隔符是保留的特殊 token 而不是字符，因此结构和内容使用词表中互不重叠的部分。标签写在每个片段的开头，片段之间的边界是明确的。嵌套结构在局部写明，模型不必在长跨度上记住层级关系。 考虑到多数团队已有基于 JSON 的流水线，团队提供了转换工具和示例 notebook，可以在 JSON 和 LLMON 之间无损互转。 ## 与对话模板的关系：在角色之外再标出“每一块是什么” LLMON 不替代对话模板（chat template），它在对话模板之上补充信息。常规对话模板告诉模型哪部分属于哪个角色（system、user、assistant）；LLMON 还告诉模型每个成分是什么意思，以及成分之间在角色内、跨角色的关系。 预览模型自带对话模板，开发者照常构造传给任何对话模型的 `messages` 列表，再照常调用 `apply_chat_template`。唯一的区别是，一个轮次可以给自己的各部分命名，并把每部分标为 `exec`: `True` 或 `False`。标为 `True` 的部分会被绑定进渲染结果底部的 `exec` 块，这个块写明要执行哪条指令、作用于什么；标为 `False` 的部分仍会渲染进上下文，但没有任何地方引用它。博客给出的例子是： ``` messages = [ { "role": "user", "instruction": [{ "value": "Write a short paragraph about", "exec": True }], "data": [{ "value": "IBM Company", "exec": True }], "requirement": [ {"value": "Use less than 10 words", "exec": True}, {"value": "Do not use commas", "exec": True}] } ] ``` 模型实际收到的是下面这段（为便于阅读加了换行和缩进，模板本身不输出这些）： ``` <|open|>instr<|:|>»ñ<|close|>Write a short paragraph about<|open_end|> <|open|>data<|:|>ä¦<|close|>IBM Company<|open_end|> <|open|>req<|:|>Á¼<|close|>Use less than 10 words<|open_end|> <|open|>req<|:|>¢¬<|close|>Do not use commas<|open_end|> <|open|>exec<|:|>ÄÐ<|close|> <|open|>exec<|.|>instruction<|close|>instr<|:|>»ñ<|open_end|> <|open|>exec<|.|>input<|close|>data<|:|>ä¦<|open_end|> <|open|>exec<|.|>requirement<|close|>req<|:|>Á¼<|open_end|> <|open|>exec<|.|>requirement<|close|>req<|:|>¢¬<|open_end|> <|open|>exec<|.|>output<|close|>assistant<|:|>ãø<|open_end|> <|open_end|> <|open|>assistant<|:|>ãø<|close|> ``` 两字符的块 ID 取自一个固定集合，这个分词器把其中每个 ID 都编码成单个 token，所以无论抽到哪个 ID，指向一个块总是只花两个 token。 角色仍然是一个 user 轮次，但它的成分以五个可单独寻址的块进入模型，由第六个块（exec 块）绑在一起。exec 块说的是：对这份数据执行这条指令，满足这两条要求，把答案写进这里指定的块，也就是模型随后填写的那个 assistant 块。按常规模板，这些成分会被拼成一个字符串，模型得自己推断哪部分是任务、哪部分是对象、哪部分是约束。 ## 提示注入测试：比测试过的最好的前沿模型多挡住 47% 的攻击 间接提示注入是把恶意指令藏在数据载荷里的攻击，载荷可能是检索到的文档、工具返回或用户提供的数据。LLMON 的指令与数据分离针对的正是这个问题。 团队把 LLMON 预览模型和若干开源、闭源模型做了对比，评测基准是 [OPI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.12815)，它把注入放进经典 NLP 任务的数据里，并使用多种攻击策略。报告的指标是稳健性，定义为 1 减去攻击成功率，也就是模型没有执行注入指令的攻击占比。 ![OPI]() 结果显示，所有非 LLMON 模型都高度易受攻击，执行注入指令的概率很高。在这个基准上 LLMON 基本消除了问题：相对团队测试过的最好的前沿模型多挡住 47% 的攻击，相对最好的开源模型多挡住 95%。团队称在其他基准（[ASB](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.02644) 和 [StruQ](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.06363)）上观察到类似趋势。 **这些基准测的是对静态间接提示注入的稳健性**，指令与数据分离直接针对这类攻击。在多轮对话中逐步展开的自适应攻击，团队表示还在改进中。 ## 通用能力与 Granite 4.1 Instruct 持平 团队称安全性的提升没有以通用能力为代价：在各类标准基准上，LLMON 模型与 Granite 4.1 Instruct 模型表现相当。 ![Granite-4.1 vs LLMON]() 按团队的说法，如果正在试用 Granite 4.1 3B 或 8B，可以直接换成 LLMON 预览版，通用性能应当相近，而对提示注入的抵抗力强得多。不需要转换流水线，像上面的例子那样给轮次的各部分命名（instruction、data、requirement）就够了，自带的对话模板会把它们转成 LLMON 块。LLMON-converters 库更进一步：如果某个部分本身是结构化的，比如一份 JSON 文档，转换后会保留它的结构，变成带类型、可单独寻址的块，而不是一个不透明的字符串。 ## 训练方法：在后训练阶段学会只认 exec 块 模型从 [Granite 4.1](https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-4.1-8b-base) 基础检查点出发，而不是从已发布的 Instruct 模型出发，因此 LLMON 行为是在后训练中学到的，没有叠加在现有对话格式之上。 LLMON 定义了六个分隔符，用来标记标签的开始和结束，并支持嵌套和锚定；它们作为保留的单个 token 装进分词器。团队把一份常规指令微调语料重新序列化成 LLMON：每个提示成分变成自己的可寻址块，每个轮次带一个执行块，写明运行哪条指令、作用于哪些输入、输出写到哪里。任务构成与普通 Instruct 模型相同（对话、多轮、RAG、工具调用），团队认为这正是基准表现与常规微调模型接近的原因。 此外，团队在数据里加入诱饵指令和诱饵数据块：它们出现在上下文中，但刻意不被绑定，目标输出保持不变。模型由此学会遵循执行块规定的依赖关系，忽略其余部分。之后是强化学习：五个连续的 GRPO 阶段，涵盖多领域推理、RLHF、知识校准和数学，最后是一个 DPO 阶段，使用一千对在线策略（on-policy）偏好样本，样本来自模型自己对注入尝试的回应。 由此形成的权限规则来自这种布局本身，而不是额外加装的护栏：经由执行块到达的指令具有权威性；作为输入到达的内容（数据、文档、工具模式、工具结果）只是要阅读的材料，不是要执行的命令。执行块没有调用的指令和数据片段会被忽略。**团队特别说明，这是一种学到的行为，不是强制保证。** 想看它在 LLMON 模型注意力层中的表现，可以试用 Hugging Face Spaces 上的 [LLMON Attention Visualization](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ibm-granite/LLMON-Attention-Visualization)。 ![Attention Demo]() ## 自定义词表：以 ScienceWorld 为例 LLMON 不绑定固定模式，可以按自己的领域选标签名和结构，再微调一个适配器来读写它们。团队在 ScienceWorld 上做了演示，这是一个文字类基准，智能体一次发出一条命令完成小学科学任务（比如把水烧开），由模拟器打分。 团队定义了一套描述解题规划轨迹结构的词表，标签包括 `instr.task.goal`、`req.planning_policy.rule`、`data.state.room`、`data.state.inventory` 和 `assistant.next_action`。他们用这些标签渲染 ScienceWorld 参考解法的每一步，在 LLMON 模型上微调了一个 LoRA。训练后的模型去玩留出的测试局，并用新词表写出下一步动作。[这个 notebook](https://github.com/generative-computing/llmon/blob/main/llmon/examples/lora-finetuning/byo-vocab_LoRA_scienceworld.ipynb) 演示了完整流程，从转换参考轨迹、玩测试局，到把适配器与未训练的基础模型对比打分；面向工具调用智能体的例子在[另一个 notebook](https://github.com/generative-computing/llmon/blob/main/llmon/examples/lora-finetuning/byo-vocab_LoRA_for_agents.ipynb) 里。博客没有给出这个 ScienceWorld 实验的分数。 ## 现在可以怎么试 团队强调这是实验性预览，适合探索和评估，**还不适合生产环境**。 - 模型：[granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview](https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-4.1-3b-llmon-preview) 和 [granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview](https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-4.1-8b-llmon-preview) - 可视化演示：[LLMON Attention Visualization](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ibm-granite/LLMON-Attention-Visualization) - LLMON 仓库： - Mellea： - 论文：、 团队欢迎使用者在 GitHub Discussions 里反馈哪些有效、哪些出了问题，以及希望看到哪些用例。做 RAG 或工具调用、担心间接提示注入的团队，可以先在自己的注入样本上对比 LLMON 预览模型和现用模型；同时要记住，已公布的结果覆盖的是静态注入，多轮自适应攻击仍在改进中。", "html": "

大语言模型靠上下文生成下一批 token。在一段很长的交互里，上下文会塞满各种成分：系统提示、过去的对话轮次、作用于检索文档的指令、工具返回或用户数据、限制输出的要求，以及推理链。IBM Granite 团队在 Hugging Face 博客上指出，这些成分本来有丰富的结构，但大多要么只是隐含在模型里，要么用 JSON 这类并非为大模型设计的格式表达。团队认为，这是大模型（尤其是较小的模型）脆弱、会以意想不到的方式出错的主要原因之一；结构不明确也会被攻击者利用，比如提示注入。

为此，团队开发了 LLMON（LLM Object Notation，读作 “lemon”），一种面向大模型的原生标记语言，用来把结构和语义明确地告诉模型。语义上连贯的成分用有意义的标签标记，标签外面包着保留的特殊 token 分隔符。数据模式（包括嵌套）以因果语言模型不会误解的方式写明。每个块有唯一 ID，可以指向上下文中任意位置的某条指令，并把它绑定到该指令要处理的数据上，类似编程语言里调用函数并传入参数。

团队同时发布了两个基于 Granite 4.1 基础模型、经训练可以读写 LLMON 标记文本的实验性预览模型：granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview 和 granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview，以及一个 GitHub 仓库，内含处理 LLMON 的工具包和工作流、模板示例。

团队给出的四项用途

  • 抵御间接提示注入。 藏在用户数据里的注入指令，大多会被 LLMON 模型忽略，因为指令和数据是明确分开的。在部分基准上攻击成功率降到接近零，而常规指令微调模型被劫持的概率很高。团队称这是在保持与 Granite 4.1 Instruct 模型相当的通用能力的前提下做到的。
  • 不串味。 每条指令都绑定到它要处理的确切数据，无关段落、旧的对话轮次和工具输出不会被拉进答案。
  • 应用代码里的结构可以被模型利用。 指令、数据和要求都有清楚的标记。可以在 Mellea 里试用，它会自动把大模型调用转成 LLMON，原生支持这种格式。
  • 不用再逼模型遵守 JSON 结构。 团队提供的转换器可以把现有 JSON 无损转成 LLMON；也可以自定义结构和标签，在 LLMON 模型上微调一个 LoRA 来理解它们。

为什么不用 JSON

JSON 是为解析器设计的，不是为因果语言模型设计的。分词器不受语法约束，而结构是靠 {、"、: 这些在普通文本里也会出现的 token 表达的。在模型眼里，文档里的一个引号和结束一个字段的引号是同一个 token。解析器眼中清清楚楚的转义规则，在模型那里只是统计规律。嵌套深度靠数括号来体现，而 Transformer 在这方面已知较弱，跨度越长越明显。

LLMON 是一种类 XML 的标记，它的结构分隔符是保留的特殊 token 而不是字符，因此结构和内容使用词表中互不重叠的部分。标签写在每个片段的开头，片段之间的边界是明确的。嵌套结构在局部写明，模型不必在长跨度上记住层级关系。

考虑到多数团队已有基于 JSON 的流水线，团队提供了转换工具和示例 notebook，可以在 JSON 和 LLMON 之间无损互转。

与对话模板的关系：在角色之外再标出“每一块是什么”

LLMON 不替代对话模板（chat template），它在对话模板之上补充信息。常规对话模板告诉模型哪部分属于哪个角色（system、user、assistant）；LLMON 还告诉模型每个成分是什么意思，以及成分之间在角色内、跨角色的关系。

预览模型自带对话模板，开发者照常构造传给任何对话模型的 messages 列表，再照常调用 apply_chat_template。唯一的区别是，一个轮次可以给自己的各部分命名，并把每部分标为 exec: True 或 False。标为 True 的部分会被绑定进渲染结果底部的 exec 块，这个块写明要执行哪条指令、作用于什么；标为 False 的部分仍会渲染进上下文，但没有任何地方引用它。博客给出的例子是：

messages = [ { "role": "user",
               "instruction": [{ "value": "Write a short paragraph about", "exec": True }],
               "data": [{ "value": "IBM Company", "exec": True }],
               "requirement": [ {"value": "Use less than 10 words", "exec": True},
                                {"value": "Do not use commas", "exec": True}]
             } ]

模型实际收到的是下面这段（为便于阅读加了换行和缩进，模板本身不输出这些）：

<|open|>instr<|:|>»ñ<|close|>Write a short paragraph about<|open_end|>
<|open|>data<|:|>ä¦<|close|>IBM Company<|open_end|>
<|open|>req<|:|>Á¼<|close|>Use less than 10 words<|open_end|>
<|open|>req<|:|>¢¬<|close|>Do not use commas<|open_end|>
<|open|>exec<|:|>ÄÐ<|close|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>instruction<|close|>instr<|:|>»ñ<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>input<|close|>data<|:|>ä¦<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>requirement<|close|>req<|:|>Á¼<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>requirement<|close|>req<|:|>¢¬<|open_end|>
    <|open|>exec<|.|>output<|close|>assistant<|:|>ãø<|open_end|>
<|open_end|>
<|open|>assistant<|:|>ãø<|close|>

两字符的块 ID 取自一个固定集合，这个分词器把其中每个 ID 都编码成单个 token，所以无论抽到哪个 ID，指向一个块总是只花两个 token。

角色仍然是一个 user 轮次，但它的成分以五个可单独寻址的块进入模型，由第六个块（exec 块）绑在一起。exec 块说的是：对这份数据执行这条指令，满足这两条要求，把答案写进这里指定的块，也就是模型随后填写的那个 assistant 块。按常规模板，这些成分会被拼成一个字符串，模型得自己推断哪部分是任务、哪部分是对象、哪部分是约束。

提示注入测试：比测试过的最好的前沿模型多挡住 47% 的攻击

间接提示注入是把恶意指令藏在数据载荷里的攻击，载荷可能是检索到的文档、工具返回或用户提供的数据。LLMON 的指令与数据分离针对的正是这个问题。

团队把 LLMON 预览模型和若干开源、闭源模型做了对比，评测基准是 OPI，它把注入放进经典 NLP 任务的数据里，并使用多种攻击策略。报告的指标是稳健性，定义为 1 减去攻击成功率，也就是模型没有执行注入指令的攻击占比。

结果显示，所有非 LLMON 模型都高度易受攻击，执行注入指令的概率很高。在这个基准上 LLMON 基本消除了问题：相对团队测试过的最好的前沿模型多挡住 47% 的攻击，相对最好的开源模型多挡住 95%。团队称在其他基准（ASB 和 StruQ）上观察到类似趋势。

这些基准测的是对静态间接提示注入的稳健性，指令与数据分离直接针对这类攻击。在多轮对话中逐步展开的自适应攻击，团队表示还在改进中。

通用能力与 Granite 4.1 Instruct 持平

团队称安全性的提升没有以通用能力为代价：在各类标准基准上，LLMON 模型与 Granite 4.1 Instruct 模型表现相当。

按团队的说法，如果正在试用 Granite 4.1 3B 或 8B，可以直接换成 LLMON 预览版，通用性能应当相近，而对提示注入的抵抗力强得多。不需要转换流水线，像上面的例子那样给轮次的各部分命名（instruction、data、requirement）就够了，自带的对话模板会把它们转成 LLMON 块。LLMON-converters 库更进一步：如果某个部分本身是结构化的，比如一份 JSON 文档，转换后会保留它的结构，变成带类型、可单独寻址的块，而不是一个不透明的字符串。

训练方法：在后训练阶段学会只认 exec 块

模型从 Granite 4.1 基础检查点出发，而不是从已发布的 Instruct 模型出发，因此 LLMON 行为是在后训练中学到的，没有叠加在现有对话格式之上。

LLMON 定义了六个分隔符，用来标记标签的开始和结束，并支持嵌套和锚定；它们作为保留的单个 token 装进分词器。团队把一份常规指令微调语料重新序列化成 LLMON：每个提示成分变成自己的可寻址块，每个轮次带一个执行块，写明运行哪条指令、作用于哪些输入、输出写到哪里。任务构成与普通 Instruct 模型相同（对话、多轮、RAG、工具调用），团队认为这正是基准表现与常规微调模型接近的原因。

此外，团队在数据里加入诱饵指令和诱饵数据块：它们出现在上下文中，但刻意不被绑定，目标输出保持不变。模型由此学会遵循执行块规定的依赖关系，忽略其余部分。之后是强化学习：五个连续的 GRPO 阶段，涵盖多领域推理、RLHF、知识校准和数学，最后是一个 DPO 阶段，使用一千对在线策略（on-policy）偏好样本，样本来自模型自己对注入尝试的回应。

由此形成的权限规则来自这种布局本身，而不是额外加装的护栏：经由执行块到达的指令具有权威性；作为输入到达的内容（数据、文档、工具模式、工具结果）只是要阅读的材料，不是要执行的命令。执行块没有调用的指令和数据片段会被忽略。团队特别说明，这是一种学到的行为，不是强制保证。 想看它在 LLMON 模型注意力层中的表现，可以试用 Hugging Face Spaces 上的 LLMON Attention Visualization。

自定义词表：以 ScienceWorld 为例

LLMON 不绑定固定模式，可以按自己的领域选标签名和结构，再微调一个适配器来读写它们。团队在 ScienceWorld 上做了演示，这是一个文字类基准，智能体一次发出一条命令完成小学科学任务（比如把水烧开），由模拟器打分。

团队定义了一套描述解题规划轨迹结构的词表，标签包括 instr.task.goal、req.planning_policy.rule、data.state.room、data.state.inventory 和 assistant.next_action。他们用这些标签渲染 ScienceWorld 参考解法的每一步，在 LLMON 模型上微调了一个 LoRA。训练后的模型去玩留出的测试局，并用新词表写出下一步动作。这个 notebook 演示了完整流程，从转换参考轨迹、玩测试局，到把适配器与未训练的基础模型对比打分；面向工具调用智能体的例子在另一个 notebook 里。博客没有给出这个 ScienceWorld 实验的分数。

现在可以怎么试

团队强调这是实验性预览，适合探索和评估，还不适合生产环境。

  • 模型：granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview 和 granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview
  • 可视化演示：LLMON Attention Visualization
  • LLMON 仓库：https://github.com/generative-computing/llmon
  • Mellea：https://github.com/generative-computing/mellea
  • 论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38120、https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.22519

团队欢迎使用者在 GitHub Discussions 里反馈哪些有效、哪些出了问题，以及希望看到哪些用例。做 RAG 或工具调用、担心间接提示注入的团队，可以先在自己的注入样本上对比 LLMON 预览模型和现用模型；同时要记住，已公布的结果覆盖的是静态注入，多轮自适应攻击仍在改进中。

item.title: 不用数据库服务器做本地分析：SQLRooms 作者讲 DuckDB 在浏览器和桌面端的用法
item.author: Ilya Boyandin, Geertjan Wielenga, Tim Cox
item.description:
DuckDB 官方博客访谈 Ilya Boyandin：从 Flowmap City 的 DuckDB-Wasm，到 Foursquare Spatial Desktop 的按需切片、Cosmograph 的百万级图谱和让 AI 写 SQL，数据都留在用户机器上。

中文改写

DuckDB 官方博客发布了一篇用户访谈，主角是 SQLRooms 的作者 Ilya Boyandin。他的做法是把分析查询放在用户自己的浏览器或电脑上，用 DuckDB 代替远程数据库服务器：交互式地图、图谱探索，以及 AI 辅助分析，数据都可以留在本机。文章由 Ilya Boyandin、Geertjan Wielenga 和 Tim Cox 署名。

Ilya 对本地数据的态度很明确，原话的意思是：你应该拥有自己的数据。数据可以放在你自己的电脑上，不是所有东西都必须放在云端。它可以通过云同步，但什么时候留在本地、什么时候不留，由你决定。

Ilya Boyandin 是一名软件工程师，做过 SQLRooms、FlowmapBlue 和 Flowmap City。他曾在 Unfolded 做地理空间数据分析，这家公司由开源可视化项目 deck.gl 和 kepler.gl 背后的团队创立，后来被 Foursquare 收购。

起点：一个预算很少的副业项目

Ilya 第一次用 DuckDB，是在 Flowmap City 里。这是一个可视化人员出行流动的副业项目，他至今还在维护。

项目预算很少，Ilya 希望它运维简单、基础设施尽量少。DuckDB 的 WebAssembly 版本让应用可以在用户浏览器里直接跑分析查询，不需要数据库服务器。用户上传的数据集以 Parquet 文件存放在 S3 上；有人打开项目时，应用通过预签名 URL 把数据加载进 DuckDB-Wasm。

用户在 Flowmap City 里平移、缩放或修改筛选条件时，DuckDB-Wasm 会在浏览器里执行 SQL 查询来更新地图。一次交互就可能触发好几条查询，为当前视口准备数据。

Ilya 的解释是：“现在我们可以在浏览器里完成大部分分析和可视化。这让基础设施需求保持在低位，而且可能更快，因为查询不需要往返服务器。”

从副业项目抽出 SQLRooms

Flowmap City 里有不少数据加载和界面代码，用处并不限于出行分析。Ilya 把这些部分抽出来，做成了 SQLRooms，并继续作为开源项目开发。

SQLRooms 是一个模块化工具包，用于在 React 里构建由 DuckDB 驱动的分析应用。它提供加载数据、编写 SQL、展示表格、制作可视化和接入 AI 助手的构件，开发者可以把这些构件和自己的组件组合使用。

这些组件在一个 Room 里协同工作。Room 是一个工作区，包含数据集、分析产物（比如保存的查询、图表、地图和文档），以及把它们连在一起的应用状态。SQLRooms 通过一个共享的 DuckDB 连接负责执行查询，开发者可以把精力放在用户如何探索数据、如何在已有工作上继续推进。

DuckDB 既可以通过 WebAssembly 直接在浏览器里运行，也可以在桌面应用里以原生方式运行在用户电脑上，两种方式都不需要远程数据库服务器。

Ilya 对本地优先（local-first）软件的兴趣，塑造了这个框架的形态，也就是开头那段关于“拥有自己的数据”的话。

在 Foursquare 落到桌面应用

在 Foursquare，Ilya 的团队一直在开发 Foursquare Spatial Desktop。这是一个用 SQLRooms 构建的地理空间数据探索桌面应用，把 DuckDB 的分析引擎和 kepler.gl 的可视化工具结合在一起。它建立在团队做 kepler.gl 和 Foursquare Studio（Foursquare 的云端地理空间分析平台）的经验之上。

Ilya 说：“对这个产品来说，把 DuckDB 嵌入桌面应用再合适不过。它让用户可以在本地执行分析流程。” 他也提到，SQLite 同样可以嵌入，但它不是列式存储，设计初衷也不是针对较大数据集做分析。

Ilya 补充说，现在的笔记本电脑算力可观，GPU 也很适合做可视化。“我看到人们重新对那种把数据和计算留在用户自己机器上的应用产生兴趣。”

按需生成地图瓦片

Spatial Desktop 用 deck.gl 渲染地图，但一次画几百万个要素会拖慢速度。应用的办法是用 DuckDB 的空间扩展做动态切片。

地图瓦片通常会提前生成好，以便快速加载。Spatial Desktop 还能用本地 DuckDB 数据库，根据用户自己的数据集按需生成瓦片，这样用户不用先准备瓦片集就能开始探索。对每个被请求的瓦片，它会选出附近的要素，并随机抽样，让密集的瓦片保持在可处理的规模；它还会按缩放级别简化线和多边形，用户放大得越多，保留的细节越多。

下面这段简化后的查询展示了主要步骤。它假设源几何数据已经是 Web Mercator 坐标（EPSG:3857）。瓦片宽度同时决定两件事：搜索范围外围的一小圈缓冲区，以及大约相当于半个像素的简化容差。

WITH tile AS (
    SELECT
        ST_TileEnvelope(z, x, y) AS bounds,
        (ST_XMax(bounds) - ST_XMin(bounds)) / 256.0 AS meters_per_pixel
),
candidates AS (
    SELECT
        f.id, f.geometry, tile.bounds,
        GREATEST(meters_per_pixel * 0.5, 0.1) AS tolerance
    FROM features f, tile
    WHERE ST_Intersects_Extent(
        f.geometry,
        ST_Buffer(tile.bounds, meters_per_pixel * 16)
    )
),
sampled AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM candidates
    USING SAMPLE reservoir(50000 ROWS)
),
encoded AS (
    SELECT
        id,
        ST_AsMVTGeom(
            ST_SimplifyPreserveTopology(geometry, tolerance),
            ST_Extent(bounds)
        ) AS geom
    FROM sampled
)
SELECT ST_AsMVT(encoded, 'features') AS tile
FROM encoded
WHERE geom IS NOT NULL;

ST_AsMVTGeom 把简化后的几何转换成瓦片坐标并做裁剪；ST_AsMVT 把这些几何及其属性打包成 Mapbox Vector Tile（MVT）。生产环境的实现还会处理无效几何、过滤掉非常小的线和多边形，并缓存已生成的瓦片。

地图请求的瓦片，由 Electron 桌面应用内部在本地运行的一个 HTTP 服务器提供。

Cosmograph：浏览器里探索百万级边的图谱

SQLRooms 也驱动着 Cosmograph 的分析工作区。Cosmograph 是一个基于浏览器的图谱探索工具，由 Nikita Rokotyan 和 Thor Whalen 开发，能可视化有数百万条边的图。Ilya 参与了把 SQLRooms 集成进这个应用的工作。

Cosmograph 测试过的数据集，从几万个点到几百万个点不等。DuckDB-Wasm 在后台 worker 里负责数据加载和 SQL 查询，帮助界面保持流畅。用户探索时，应用可以借它筛选和汇总数据；列式的查询结果也减少了为可视化准备数据所需的转换工作。

让 AI 智能体写 SQL

SQLRooms 也支持 AI 辅助分析。Ilya 说：“SQL 和 AI 智能体的组合其实相当强大。SQL 历史很长，网上有大量讲怎么用它的文档，所以大模型很擅长生成 SQL。”

用户可以用自然语言提问。助手生成 SQL 查询和图表规格，由应用在本地执行和渲染。源数据集可以留在用户电脑上，只把数据库结构和部分选定的查询结果发给 AI 服务商，帮助回答问题。

在下面这个 Spatial Desktop 示例里，助手生成 SQL，从可用数据源取数，并计算意大利各地适合种植葡萄的综合评分。生成的地图旁边附有 AI 生成的分区域分析。

SQLRooms 的下一步

Ilya 正在扩展 SQLRooms 的工作区模型，让用户可以把分析汇总到交互式文档里。这些文档把文字和图表、SQL 查询等区块组合在一起，用户可以在产出结论的分析旁边直接解释自己的发现。

Ilya 也在探索使用这些分析项目的其他方式。在阿姆斯特丹举办的 DuckCon #7 上，他演示了一个带笔记本式界面的 SQLRooms 命令行工具，它把数据和分析产物都保存在同一个 DuckDB 数据库文件里。目标是让用户可以在图形应用和命令行之间切换，继续同一个项目。这个 CLI 的设计仍在演变中。

延伸阅读

Ilya 在 DuckCon #7 上有一个五分钟的演讲，简要介绍了这个方向。

SQLRooms 是开源的，地址是 sqlrooms.org，可以从它的示例页入手。Flowmap City、Foursquare Spatial Desktop 和 Cosmograph 都可以免费试用。Ilya 关于 DuckDB 和 SQLRooms 的文章发布在他的个人网站上。

DuckDB 团队在文末感谢 Ilya 接受访谈，并邀请正在使用 DuckDB、愿意分享自己故事的读者发邮件给 geertjan@ducklabs.com。

原文附带媒体

原文附带媒体；未核验其与具体段落的对应关系。

原文

原文的题图、两张截图和四段视频已移到上方媒体区，正文中以 [Header image]、[Image N]、[Video N] 标出原位置；作者头像、目录和推荐文章等页面元素未收录；页面中被混淆显示的联系邮箱已还原为原地址。

Local Analytics Doesn’t Need a Database Server

[Header image: shown in the media section above]

TL;DR: From interactive maps to graph exploration, DuckDB makes it possible to analyze data without a database server. Ilya Boyandin shares how this approach led to SQLRooms, a toolkit for building analytics applications that bring data, visualizations, and AI-assisted analysis together on the user’s machine.

You should own your data. It can live on your computer, not everything has to live in the Cloud. It can be synced via the cloud, but you decide when to keep it local and when not.

— Ilya Boyandin, creator of SQLRooms

Ilya Boyandin is a software engineer, the creator of SQLRooms, FlowmapBlue, and Flowmap City. He worked on geospatial data analytics at Unfolded, the company founded by the team behind the open-source data visualization projects deck.gl and kepler.gl, which was later acquired by Foursquare.

How DuckDB Entered the Picture

Ilya first used DuckDB in Flowmap City, a side project for visualizing mobility flows that he still maintains. Working with a small budget, Ilya wanted to keep Flowmap City easy to operate with minimal infrastructure. DuckDB’s WebAssembly build lets the app run analytical queries in the user’s browser without a database server. Uploaded datasets are stored as Parquet files in S3. When someone opens a project, the app loads the data into DuckDB-Wasm through presigned URLs.

As users pan, zoom, or change filters in Flowmap City, DuckDB-Wasm runs SQL queries in the browser to update the map. A single interaction can trigger a number of queries preparing the data for the current viewport:

[Video 1: shown in the media section above]

Ilya explains: “We can now do much of the analysis and visualization in the browser. This keeps infrastructure requirements low and can be faster because queries don’t need a round trip to the server.”

From a Side Project to SQLRooms

Much of Flowmap City’s data-loading and interface code was useful beyond mobility analysis. Ilya extracted those pieces into SQLRooms, which he continues to develop as an open-source project.

SQLRooms is a modular toolkit for building DuckDB-powered analytics applications in React. It provides building blocks for loading data, writing SQL, displaying tables, creating visualizations, and integrating AI assistants. Developers can combine these pieces with their own components.

These components work together within a Room: a workspace containing datasets, analysis artifacts such as saved queries, charts, maps, and documents, and the application state that connects them. SQLRooms handles query execution through a shared DuckDB connection, so developers can focus on how users explore their data and build on their work.

DuckDB can run directly in the browser through WebAssembly or natively on the user’s machine in a desktop application, allowing data analysis without a remote database server.

Ilya’s interest in local-first software shaped the framework. “You should own your data. It can live on your computer, not everything has to live in the Cloud. It can be synced via the cloud, but you decide when to keep it local and when not.”

Putting SQLRooms to Work at Foursquare

At Foursquare, Ilya’s team has been developing Foursquare Spatial Desktop, a desktop application for exploring geospatial data built with SQLRooms. It combines DuckDB’s analytical engine with kepler.gl’s visualization tools. The app builds on the team’s experience with kepler.gl and Foursquare Studio, its cloud-hosted geospatial analytics platform.

Ilya explains: “For this particular product, DuckDB embedded into the desktop app is just the perfect fit. It enables analysis workflows which users can execute locally.” SQLite is embeddable too, he says, but it is not column-oriented and was not designed for analytics on larger datasets.

[Image 1: shown in the media section above]

Modern laptops have substantial computing power and GPUs well suited to visualization, Ilya adds. “I’m seeing renewed interest in applications that keep data and computation on the user’s own machine.”

Dynamic Tiling in Spatial Desktop

Spatial Desktop uses deck.gl to render maps, but drawing millions of features at once can slow things down. The app addresses this with dynamic tiling powered by DuckDB’s spatial extension.

Map tiles are often prepared in advance for fast loading. Spatial Desktop can also generate tiles from users’ own datasets on demand, using the local DuckDB database, so users can start exploring without preparing a tileset first. For each requested tile, it selects nearby features and takes a random sample to keep dense tiles manageable. It also simplifies lines and polygons according to the zoom level, retaining more detail as the user zooms in.

[Video 2: shown in the media section above]

The following simplified query shows the main steps. It assumes the source geometries are already in Web Mercator coordinates (EPSG:3857). The tile width determines both a small buffer around the search area and a simplification tolerance equivalent to roughly half a pixel:

WITH tile AS (
    SELECT
        ST_TileEnvelope(z, x, y) AS bounds,
        (ST_XMax(bounds) - ST_XMin(bounds)) / 256.0 AS meters_per_pixel
),
candidates AS (
    SELECT
        f.id, f.geometry, tile.bounds,
        GREATEST(meters_per_pixel * 0.5, 0.1) AS tolerance
    FROM features f, tile
    WHERE ST_Intersects_Extent(
        f.geometry,
        ST_Buffer(tile.bounds, meters_per_pixel * 16)
    )
),
sampled AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM candidates
    USING SAMPLE reservoir(50000 ROWS)
),
encoded AS (
    SELECT
        id,
        ST_AsMVTGeom(
            ST_SimplifyPreserveTopology(geometry, tolerance),
            ST_Extent(bounds)
        ) AS geom
    FROM sampled
)
SELECT ST_AsMVT(encoded, 'features') AS tile
FROM encoded
WHERE geom IS NOT NULL;

ST_AsMVTGeom converts the simplified geometries to tile coordinates and clips them; ST_AsMVT packages them and their attributes into a Mapbox Vector Tile (MVT). The production implementation also handles invalid geometries, filters out very small lines and polygons, and caches generated tiles.

An HTTP server running locally as part of the Electron desktop app serves the tiles requested by the map.

Graph Analytics on the Fly with Cosmograph

SQLRooms also powers the analytical workspace in Cosmograph, a browser-based graph exploration tool developed by Nikita Rokotyan and Thor Whalen. Ilya helped integrate SQLRooms into the application, which can visualize graphs with millions of edges.

[Video 3: shown in the media section above]

Cosmograph has been tested with datasets ranging from tens of thousands of points to several million. DuckDB-Wasm handles data loading and SQL queries in a background worker, helping keep the interface responsive. It lets the app filter and summarize data as users explore, while columnar query results reduce the conversion work needed to prepare data for visualization.

When the Agent Writes the SQL

SQLRooms also supports AI-assisted analysis. “The combination of SQL and AI agents is actually quite powerful,” Ilya says. “SQL has a long history, there are many documents on the web explaining how to use it, so LLMs are pretty good at generating it.”

Users can ask questions in natural language. The assistant generates SQL queries and chart specifications, which the application executes and renders locally. The source dataset can stay on the user’s machine, while database schemas and selected query results can be shared with the AI provider to help answer questions.

In the Spatial Desktop example below, the assistant generates SQL to retrieve data from available sources and calculate a combined score for wine-growing suitability across Italy. The resulting map is accompanied by AI-generated regional analysis:

[Image 2: shown in the media section above]

Where SQLRooms Goes Next

Ilya is extending SQLRooms’ workspace model so users can bring their analysis together in interactive documents. These documents combine text with blocks such as charts or SQL queries, letting users explain their findings alongside the analysis that produced them.

[Video 4: shown in the media section above]

Ilya is also exploring other ways to work with these analytical projects. At DuckCon #7 in Amsterdam, he demonstrated a SQLRooms command-line tool with a notebook-style interface. It saves both the data and the analysis artifacts in a single DuckDB database file. The goal is to let users continue the same project through a graphical application or the command line. The CLI design is still evolving.

Learn More

Ilya’s five-minute talk from DuckCon #7 gives a short tour of this direction.

SQLRooms is open source and available at sqlrooms.org. Its examples page is a good place to start. Flowmap City, Foursquare Spatial Desktop, and Cosmograph are free to try.

We would like to thank Ilya for the conversation. You can follow his writing on DuckDB and SQLRooms on his website. And if you are reading this, are using DuckDB, and would like to share your story, drop us a line at geertjan@ducklabs.com.

相关链接：https://sqlrooms.org

DuckDB 官方博客访谈 Ilya Boyandin：从 Flowmap City 的 DuckDB-Wasm，到 Foursquare Spatial Desktop 的按需切片、Cosmograph 的百万级图谱和让 AI 写 SQL，数据都留在用户机器上。

中文改写

DuckDB 官方博客发布了一篇用户访谈，主角是 SQLRooms 的作者 Ilya Boyandin。他的做法是把分析查询放在用户自己的浏览器或电脑上，用 DuckDB 代替远程数据库服务器：交互式地图、图谱探索，以及 AI 辅助分析，数据都可以留在本机。文章由 Ilya Boyandin、Geertjan Wielenga 和 Tim Cox 署名。

Ilya 对本地数据的态度很明确，原话的意思是：你应该拥有自己的数据。数据可以放在你自己的电脑上，不是所有东西都必须放在云端。它可以通过云同步，但什么时候留在本地、什么时候不留，由你决定。

Ilya Boyandin 是一名软件工程师，做过 SQLRooms、FlowmapBlue 和 Flowmap City。他曾在 Unfolded 做地理空间数据分析，这家公司由开源可视化项目 deck.gl 和 kepler.gl 背后的团队创立，后来被 Foursquare 收购。

起点：一个预算很少的副业项目

Ilya 第一次用 DuckDB，是在 Flowmap City 里。这是一个可视化人员出行流动的副业项目，他至今还在维护。

项目预算很少，Ilya 希望它运维简单、基础设施尽量少。DuckDB 的 WebAssembly 版本让应用可以在用户浏览器里直接跑分析查询，不需要数据库服务器。用户上传的数据集以 Parquet 文件存放在 S3 上；有人打开项目时，应用通过预签名 URL 把数据加载进 DuckDB-Wasm。

用户在 Flowmap City 里平移、缩放或修改筛选条件时，DuckDB-Wasm 会在浏览器里执行 SQL 查询来更新地图。一次交互就可能触发好几条查询，为当前视口准备数据。

Ilya 的解释是：“现在我们可以在浏览器里完成大部分分析和可视化。这让基础设施需求保持在低位，而且可能更快，因为查询不需要往返服务器。”

从副业项目抽出 SQLRooms

Flowmap City 里有不少数据加载和界面代码，用处并不限于出行分析。Ilya 把这些部分抽出来，做成了 SQLRooms，并继续作为开源项目开发。

SQLRooms 是一个模块化工具包，用于在 React 里构建由 DuckDB 驱动的分析应用。它提供加载数据、编写 SQL、展示表格、制作可视化和接入 AI 助手的构件，开发者可以把这些构件和自己的组件组合使用。

这些组件在一个 Room 里协同工作。Room 是一个工作区，包含数据集、分析产物（比如保存的查询、图表、地图和文档），以及把它们连在一起的应用状态。SQLRooms 通过一个共享的 DuckDB 连接负责执行查询，开发者可以把精力放在用户如何探索数据、如何在已有工作上继续推进。

DuckDB 既可以通过 WebAssembly 直接在浏览器里运行，也可以在桌面应用里以原生方式运行在用户电脑上，两种方式都不需要远程数据库服务器。

Ilya 对本地优先（local-first）软件的兴趣，塑造了这个框架的形态，也就是开头那段关于“拥有自己的数据”的话。

SQLRooms 是开源的，地址是 sqlrooms.org，可以从它的示例页入手。Flowmap City、Foursquare Spatial Desktop 和 Cosmograph 都可以免费试用。Ilya 关于 DuckDB 和 SQLRooms 的文章发布在他的个人网站上。

DuckDB 团队在文末感谢 Ilya 接受访谈，并邀请正在使用 DuckDB、愿意分享自己故事的读者发邮件给 geertjan@ducklabs.com。

原文附带媒体

原文附带媒体；未核验其与具体段落的对应关系。

原文

原文的题图、两张截图和四段视频已移到上方媒体区，正文中以 [Header image]、[Image N]、[Video N] 标出原位置；作者头像、目录和推荐文章等页面元素未收录；页面中被混淆显示的联系邮箱已还原为原地址。

Local Analytics Doesn’t Need a Database Server

[Header image: shown in the media section above]

TL;DR: From interactive maps to graph exploration, DuckDB makes it possible to analyze data without a database server. Ilya Boyandin shares how this approach led to SQLRooms, a toolkit for building analytics applications that bring data, visualizations, and AI-assisted analysis together on the user’s machine.

You should own your data. It can live on your computer, not everything has to live in the Cloud. It can be synced via the cloud, but you decide when to keep it local and when not.

— Ilya Boyandin, creator of SQLRooms

Ilya Boyandin is a software engineer, the creator of SQLRooms, FlowmapBlue, and Flowmap City. He worked on geospatial data analytics at Unfolded, the company founded by the team behind the open-source data visualization projects deck.gl and kepler.gl, which was later acquired by Foursquare.

How DuckDB Entered the Picture

Ilya first used DuckDB in Flowmap City, a side project for visualizing mobility flows that he still maintains. Working with a small budget, Ilya wanted to keep Flowmap City easy to operate with minimal infrastructure. DuckDB’s WebAssembly build lets the app run analytical queries in the user’s browser without a database server. Uploaded datasets are stored as Parquet files in S3. When someone opens a project, the app loads the data into DuckDB-Wasm through presigned URLs.

As users pan, zoom, or change filters in Flowmap City, DuckDB-Wasm runs SQL queries in the browser to update the map. A single interaction can trigger a number of queries preparing the data for the current viewport:

[Video 1: shown in the media section above]

Ilya explains: “We can now do much of the analysis and visualization in the browser. This keeps infrastructure requirements low and can be faster because queries don’t need a round trip to the server.”

From a Side Project to SQLRooms

Much of Flowmap City’s data-loading and interface code was useful beyond mobility analysis. Ilya extracted those pieces into SQLRooms, which he continues to develop as an open-source project.

SQLRooms is a modular toolkit for building DuckDB-powered analytics applications in React. It provides building blocks for loading data, writing SQL, displaying tables, creating visualizations, and integrating AI assistants. Developers can combine these pieces with their own components.

These components work together within a Room: a workspace containing datasets, analysis artifacts such as saved queries, charts, maps, and documents, and the application state that connects them. SQLRooms handles query execution through a shared DuckDB connection, so developers can focus on how users explore their data and build on their work.

DuckDB can run directly in the browser through WebAssembly or natively on the user’s machine in a desktop application, allowing data analysis without a remote database server.

Ilya’s interest in local-first software shaped the framework. “You should own your data. It can live on your computer, not everything has to live in the Cloud. It can be synced via the cloud, but you decide when to keep it local and when not.”

Putting SQLRooms to Work at Foursquare

At Foursquare, Ilya’s team has been developing Foursquare Spatial Desktop, a desktop application for exploring geospatial data built with SQLRooms. It combines DuckDB’s analytical engine with kepler.gl’s visualization tools. The app builds on the team’s experience with kepler.gl and Foursquare Studio, its cloud-hosted geospatial analytics platform.

Ilya explains: “For this particular product, DuckDB embedded into the desktop app is just the perfect fit. It enables analysis workflows which users can execute locally.” SQLite is embeddable too, he says, but it is not column-oriented and was not designed for analytics on larger datasets.

[Image 1: shown in the media section above]

Modern laptops have substantial computing power and GPUs well suited to visualization, Ilya adds. “I’m seeing renewed interest in applications that keep data and computation on the user’s own machine.”

Dynamic Tiling in Spatial Desktop

Spatial Desktop uses deck.gl to render maps, but drawing millions of features at once can slow things down. The app addresses this with dynamic tiling powered by DuckDB’s spatial extension.

Map tiles are often prepared in advance for fast loading. Spatial Desktop can also generate tiles from users’ own datasets on demand, using the local DuckDB database, so users can start exploring without preparing a tileset first. For each requested tile, it selects nearby features and takes a random sample to keep dense tiles manageable. It also simplifies lines and polygons according to the zoom level, retaining more detail as the user zooms in.

[Video 2: shown in the media section above]

The following simplified query shows the main steps. It assumes the source geometries are already in Web Mercator coordinates (EPSG:3857). The tile width determines both a small buffer around the search area and a simplification tolerance equivalent to roughly half a pixel:

WITH tile AS (
    SELECT
        ST_TileEnvelope(z, x, y) AS bounds,
        (ST_XMax(bounds) - ST_XMin(bounds)) / 256.0 AS meters_per_pixel
),
candidates AS (
    SELECT
        f.id, f.geometry, tile.bounds,
        GREATEST(meters_per_pixel * 0.5, 0.1) AS tolerance
    FROM features f, tile
    WHERE ST_Intersects_Extent(
        f.geometry,
        ST_Buffer(tile.bounds, meters_per_pixel * 16)
    )
),
sampled AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM candidates
    USING SAMPLE reservoir(50000 ROWS)
),
encoded AS (
    SELECT
        id,
        ST_AsMVTGeom(
            ST_SimplifyPreserveTopology(geometry, tolerance),
            ST_Extent(bounds)
        ) AS geom
    FROM sampled
)
SELECT ST_AsMVT(encoded, 'features') AS tile
FROM encoded
WHERE geom IS NOT NULL;

ST_AsMVTGeom converts the simplified geometries to tile coordinates and clips them; ST_AsMVT packages them and their attributes into a Mapbox Vector Tile (MVT). The production implementation also handles invalid geometries, filters out very small lines and polygons, and caches generated tiles.

An HTTP server running locally as part of the Electron desktop app serves the tiles requested by the map.

Graph Analytics on the Fly with Cosmograph

SQLRooms also powers the analytical workspace in Cosmograph, a browser-based graph exploration tool developed by Nikita Rokotyan and Thor Whalen. Ilya helped integrate SQLRooms into the application, which can visualize graphs with millions of edges.

[Video 3: shown in the media section above]

Cosmograph has been tested with datasets ranging from tens of thousands of points to several million. DuckDB-Wasm handles data loading and SQL queries in a background worker, helping keep the interface responsive. It lets the app filter and summarize data as users explore, while columnar query results reduce the conversion work needed to prepare data for visualization.

When the Agent Writes the SQL

SQLRooms also supports AI-assisted analysis. “The combination of SQL and AI agents is actually quite powerful,” Ilya says. “SQL has a long history, there are many documents on the web explaining how to use it, so LLMs are pretty good at generating it.”

Users can ask questions in natural language. The assistant generates SQL queries and chart specifications, which the application executes and renders locally. The source dataset can stay on the user’s machine, while database schemas and selected query results can be shared with the AI provider to help answer questions.

In the Spatial Desktop example below, the assistant generates SQL to retrieve data from available sources and calculate a combined score for wine-growing suitability across Italy. The resulting map is accompanied by AI-generated regional analysis:

[Image 2: shown in the media section above]

Where SQLRooms Goes Next

Ilya is extending SQLRooms’ workspace model so users can bring their analysis together in interactive documents. These documents combine text with blocks such as charts or SQL queries, letting users explain their findings alongside the analysis that produced them.

[Video 4: shown in the media section above]

Ilya is also exploring other ways to work with these analytical projects. At DuckCon #7 in Amsterdam, he demonstrated a SQLRooms command-line tool with a notebook-style interface. It saves both the data and the analysis artifacts in a single DuckDB database file. The goal is to let users continue the same project through a graphical application or the command line. The CLI design is still evolving.

Learn More

Ilya’s five-minute talk from DuckCon #7 gives a short tour of this direction.

SQLRooms is open source and available at sqlrooms.org. Its examples page is a good place to start. Flowmap City, Foursquare Spatial Desktop, and Cosmograph are free to try.

We would like to thank Ilya for the conversation. You can follow his writing on DuckDB and SQLRooms on his website. And if you are reading this, are using DuckDB, and would like to share your story, drop us a line at geertjan@ducklabs.com.

相关链接：https://sqlrooms.org

"}, "rewrite": {"title": "不用数据库服务器做本地分析：SQLRooms 作者讲 DuckDB 在浏览器和桌面端的用法", "markdown": "DuckDB 官方博客发布了一篇用户访谈，主角是 SQLRooms 的作者 Ilya Boyandin。他的做法是把分析查询放在用户自己的浏览器或电脑上，用 DuckDB 代替远程数据库服务器：交互式地图、图谱探索，以及 AI 辅助分析，数据都可以留在本机。文章由 Ilya Boyandin、Geertjan Wielenga 和 Tim Cox 署名。 Ilya 对本地数据的态度很明确，原话的意思是：**你应该拥有自己的数据。数据可以放在你自己的电脑上，不是所有东西都必须放在云端。它可以通过云同步，但什么时候留在本地、什么时候不留，由你决定。** [Ilya Boyandin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ilyabo/) 是一名软件工程师，做过 [SQLRooms](https://sqlrooms.org)、[FlowmapBlue](https://flowmap.blue) 和 [Flowmap City](https://flowmap.city/)。他曾在 Unfolded 做地理空间数据分析，这家公司由开源可视化项目 [deck.gl](https://deck.gl) 和 [kepler.gl](https://kepler.gl) 背后的团队创立，后来被 Foursquare 收购。 ## 起点：一个预算很少的副业项目 Ilya 第一次用 DuckDB，是在 [Flowmap City](https://flowmap.city/) 里。这是一个[可视化人员出行流动](https://ilya.boyandin.me/p/flowmap-city)的副业项目，他至今还在维护。 项目预算很少，Ilya 希望它运维简单、基础设施尽量少。DuckDB 的 [WebAssembly 版本](https://duckdb.org/docs/2.0/clients/wasm/overview.html)让应用可以在用户浏览器里直接跑分析查询，不需要数据库服务器。用户上传的数据集以 Parquet 文件存放在 S3 上；有人打开项目时，应用通过[预签名 URL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/ShareObjectPreSignedURL.html) 把数据加载进 DuckDB-Wasm。 用户在 Flowmap City 里平移、缩放或修改筛选条件时，DuckDB-Wasm 会在浏览器里执行 SQL 查询来更新地图。一次交互就可能触发好几条查询，为当前视口准备数据。 [观看原视频]() Ilya 的解释是：**“现在我们可以在浏览器里完成大部分分析和可视化。这让基础设施需求保持在低位，而且可能更快，因为查询不需要往返服务器。”** ## 从副业项目抽出 SQLRooms Flowmap City 里有不少数据加载和界面代码，用处并不限于出行分析。Ilya 把这些部分抽出来，做成了 SQLRooms，并继续作为开源项目开发。 [SQLRooms](https://sqlrooms.org/) 是一个模块化工具包，用于在 React 里构建由 DuckDB 驱动的分析应用。它提供加载数据、编写 SQL、展示表格、制作可视化和接入 AI 助手的构件，开发者可以把这些构件和自己的组件组合使用。 这些组件在一个 *Room* 里协同工作。Room 是一个工作区，包含数据集、分析产物（比如保存的查询、图表、地图和文档），以及把它们连在一起的应用状态。SQLRooms 通过一个共享的 DuckDB 连接负责执行查询，开发者可以把精力放在用户如何探索数据、如何在已有工作上继续推进。 DuckDB 既可以通过 WebAssembly 直接在浏览器里运行，也可以在桌面应用里以原生方式运行在用户电脑上，两种方式都不需要远程数据库服务器。 Ilya 对本地优先（local-first）软件的兴趣，塑造了这个框架的形态，也就是开头那段关于“拥有自己的数据”的话。 ## 在 Foursquare 落到桌面应用 在 Foursquare，Ilya 的团队一直在开发 [Foursquare Spatial Desktop](https://ilya.boyandin.me/p/fsq-spatial-desktop)。这是一个用 SQLRooms 构建的地理空间数据探索桌面应用，把 DuckDB 的分析引擎和 [kepler.gl](https://kepler.gl/) 的可视化工具结合在一起。它建立在团队做 kepler.gl 和 [Foursquare Studio](https://studio.foursquare.com)（Foursquare 的云端地理空间分析平台）的经验之上。 Ilya 说：**“对这个产品来说，把 DuckDB 嵌入桌面应用再合适不过。它让用户可以在本地执行分析流程。”** 他也提到，SQLite 同样可以嵌入，但它不是列式存储，设计初衷也不是针对较大数据集做分析。 ![Foursquare Spatial Desktop]() Ilya 补充说，现在的笔记本电脑算力可观，GPU 也很适合做可视化。**“我看到人们重新对那种把数据和计算留在用户自己机器上的应用产生兴趣。”** ### 按需生成地图瓦片 Spatial Desktop 用 [deck.gl](https://deck.gl/) 渲染地图，但一次画几百万个要素会拖慢速度。应用的办法是用 DuckDB 的[空间扩展](https://duckdb.org/docs/2.0/core_extensions/spatial/overview.html)做动态切片。 地图瓦片通常会提前生成好，以便快速加载。Spatial Desktop 还能用本地 DuckDB 数据库，根据用户自己的数据集按需生成瓦片，这样用户不用先准备瓦片集就能开始探索。对每个被请求的瓦片，它会选出附近的要素，并随机抽样，让密集的瓦片保持在可处理的规模；它还会按缩放级别简化线和多边形，用户放大得越多，保留的细节越多。 [观看原视频]() 下面这段简化后的查询展示了主要步骤。它假设源几何数据已经是 Web Mercator 坐标（`EPSG:3857`）。瓦片宽度同时决定两件事：搜索范围外围的一小圈缓冲区，以及大约相当于半个像素的简化容差。 ``` WITH tile AS ( SELECT ST_TileEnvelope(z, x, y) AS bounds, (ST_XMax(bounds) - ST_XMin(bounds)) / 256.0 AS meters_per_pixel ), candidates AS ( SELECT f.id, f.geometry, tile.bounds, GREATEST(meters_per_pixel * 0.5, 0.1) AS tolerance FROM features f, tile WHERE ST_Intersects_Extent( f.geometry, ST_Buffer(tile.bounds, meters_per_pixel * 16) ) ), sampled AS ( SELECT * FROM candidates USING SAMPLE reservoir(50000 ROWS) ), encoded AS ( SELECT id, ST_AsMVTGeom( ST_SimplifyPreserveTopology(geometry, tolerance), ST_Extent(bounds) ) AS geom FROM sampled ) SELECT ST_AsMVT(encoded, 'features') AS tile FROM encoded WHERE geom IS NOT NULL; ``` `ST_AsMVTGeom` 把简化后的几何转换成瓦片坐标并做裁剪；[`ST_AsMVT`](https://duckdb.org/docs/2.0/core_extensions/spatial/functions.html#st_asmvt) 把这些几何及其属性打包成 Mapbox Vector Tile（MVT）。生产环境的实现还会处理无效几何、过滤掉非常小的线和多边形，并缓存已生成的瓦片。 地图请求的瓦片，由 Electron 桌面应用内部在本地运行的一个 HTTP 服务器提供。 ## Cosmograph：浏览器里探索百万级边的图谱 SQLRooms 也驱动着 [Cosmograph](https://cosmograph.app) 的分析工作区。Cosmograph 是一个基于浏览器的图谱探索工具，由 [Nikita Rokotyan](https://rokotyan.com/) 和 Thor Whalen 开发，能可视化有数百万条边的图。Ilya 参与了把 SQLRooms 集成进这个应用的工作。 [观看原视频]() Cosmograph 测试过的数据集，从几万个点到几百万个点不等。DuckDB-Wasm 在后台 worker 里负责数据加载和 SQL 查询，帮助界面保持流畅。用户探索时，应用可以借它筛选和汇总数据；列式的查询结果也减少了为可视化准备数据所需的转换工作。 ## 让 AI 智能体写 SQL SQLRooms 也支持 AI 辅助分析。Ilya 说：**“SQL 和 AI 智能体的组合其实相当强大。SQL 历史很长，网上有大量讲怎么用它的文档，所以大模型很擅长生成 SQL。”** 用户可以用自然语言提问。助手生成 SQL 查询和图表规格，由应用在本地执行和渲染。源数据集可以留在用户电脑上，只把数据库结构和部分选定的查询结果发给 AI 服务商，帮助回答问题。 在下面这个 Spatial Desktop 示例里，助手生成 SQL，从可用数据源取数，并计算意大利各地适合种植葡萄的综合评分。生成的地图旁边附有 AI 生成的分区域分析。 ![Foursquare Spatial Desktop showing a wine-growing suitability map of Italy alongside AI-generated regional analysis]() ## SQLRooms 的下一步 Ilya 正在扩展 SQLRooms 的工作区模型，让用户可以把分析汇总到交互式文档里。这些文档把文字和图表、SQL 查询等区块组合在一起，用户可以在产出结论的分析旁边直接解释自己的发现。 [观看原视频]() Ilya 也在探索使用这些分析项目的其他方式。在阿姆斯特丹举办的 [DuckCon #7](https://duckdb.org/events/2026/06/24/duckcon7/) 上，他演示了一个带笔记本式界面的 SQLRooms 命令行工具，它把数据和分析产物都保存在同一个 DuckDB 数据库文件里。目标是让用户可以在图形应用和命令行之间切换，继续同一个项目。这个 CLI 的设计仍在演变中。 ## 延伸阅读 Ilya 在 DuckCon #7 上有一个[五分钟的演讲](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fV1LXnPl4ng)，简要介绍了这个方向。 SQLRooms 是开源的，地址是 [sqlrooms.org](https://sqlrooms.org)，可以从它的[示例页](https://sqlrooms.org/examples)入手。[Flowmap City](https://flowmap.city/)、[Foursquare Spatial Desktop](https://foursquare.com/products/spatial-desktop/) 和 [Cosmograph](https://cosmograph.app) 都可以免费试用。Ilya 关于 DuckDB 和 SQLRooms 的文章发布在[他的个人网站](https://ilya.boyandin.me/)上。 DuckDB 团队在文末感谢 Ilya 接受访谈，并邀请正在使用 DuckDB、愿意分享自己故事的读者发邮件给 [geertjan@ducklabs.com](mailto:geertjan@ducklabs.com)。 ### 原文附带媒体 原文附带媒体；未核验其与具体段落的对应关系。 ![原帖图片]()", "html": "

DuckDB 官方博客发布了一篇用户访谈，主角是 SQLRooms 的作者 Ilya Boyandin。他的做法是把分析查询放在用户自己的浏览器或电脑上，用 DuckDB 代替远程数据库服务器：交互式地图、图谱探索，以及 AI 辅助分析，数据都可以留在本机。文章由 Ilya Boyandin、Geertjan Wielenga 和 Tim Cox 署名。

Ilya 对本地数据的态度很明确，原话的意思是：你应该拥有自己的数据。数据可以放在你自己的电脑上，不是所有东西都必须放在云端。它可以通过云同步，但什么时候留在本地、什么时候不留，由你决定。

Ilya Boyandin 是一名软件工程师，做过 SQLRooms、FlowmapBlue 和 Flowmap City。他曾在 Unfolded 做地理空间数据分析，这家公司由开源可视化项目 deck.gl 和 kepler.gl 背后的团队创立，后来被 Foursquare 收购。

起点：一个预算很少的副业项目

Ilya 第一次用 DuckDB，是在 Flowmap City 里。这是一个可视化人员出行流动的副业项目，他至今还在维护。

项目预算很少，Ilya 希望它运维简单、基础设施尽量少。DuckDB 的 WebAssembly 版本让应用可以在用户浏览器里直接跑分析查询，不需要数据库服务器。用户上传的数据集以 Parquet 文件存放在 S3 上；有人打开项目时，应用通过预签名 URL 把数据加载进 DuckDB-Wasm。

用户在 Flowmap City 里平移、缩放或修改筛选条件时，DuckDB-Wasm 会在浏览器里执行 SQL 查询来更新地图。一次交互就可能触发好几条查询，为当前视口准备数据。

Ilya 的解释是：“现在我们可以在浏览器里完成大部分分析和可视化。这让基础设施需求保持在低位，而且可能更快，因为查询不需要往返服务器。”

从副业项目抽出 SQLRooms

Flowmap City 里有不少数据加载和界面代码，用处并不限于出行分析。Ilya 把这些部分抽出来，做成了 SQLRooms，并继续作为开源项目开发。

SQLRooms 是一个模块化工具包，用于在 React 里构建由 DuckDB 驱动的分析应用。它提供加载数据、编写 SQL、展示表格、制作可视化和接入 AI 助手的构件，开发者可以把这些构件和自己的组件组合使用。

这些组件在一个 Room 里协同工作。Room 是一个工作区，包含数据集、分析产物（比如保存的查询、图表、地图和文档），以及把它们连在一起的应用状态。SQLRooms 通过一个共享的 DuckDB 连接负责执行查询，开发者可以把精力放在用户如何探索数据、如何在已有工作上继续推进。

DuckDB 既可以通过 WebAssembly 直接在浏览器里运行，也可以在桌面应用里以原生方式运行在用户电脑上，两种方式都不需要远程数据库服务器。

Ilya 对本地优先（local-first）软件的兴趣，塑造了这个框架的形态，也就是开头那段关于“拥有自己的数据”的话。

在 Foursquare 落到桌面应用

在 Foursquare，Ilya 的团队一直在开发 Foursquare Spatial Desktop。这是一个用 SQLRooms 构建的地理空间数据探索桌面应用，把 DuckDB 的分析引擎和 kepler.gl 的可视化工具结合在一起。它建立在团队做 kepler.gl 和 Foursquare Studio（Foursquare 的云端地理空间分析平台）的经验之上。

Ilya 说：“对这个产品来说，把 DuckDB 嵌入桌面应用再合适不过。它让用户可以在本地执行分析流程。” 他也提到，SQLite 同样可以嵌入，但它不是列式存储，设计初衷也不是针对较大数据集做分析。

Ilya 补充说，现在的笔记本电脑算力可观，GPU 也很适合做可视化。“我看到人们重新对那种把数据和计算留在用户自己机器上的应用产生兴趣。”

按需生成地图瓦片

Spatial Desktop 用 deck.gl 渲染地图，但一次画几百万个要素会拖慢速度。应用的办法是用 DuckDB 的空间扩展做动态切片。

地图瓦片通常会提前生成好，以便快速加载。Spatial Desktop 还能用本地 DuckDB 数据库，根据用户自己的数据集按需生成瓦片，这样用户不用先准备瓦片集就能开始探索。对每个被请求的瓦片，它会选出附近的要素，并随机抽样，让密集的瓦片保持在可处理的规模；它还会按缩放级别简化线和多边形，用户放大得越多，保留的细节越多。

下面这段简化后的查询展示了主要步骤。它假设源几何数据已经是 Web Mercator 坐标（EPSG:3857）。瓦片宽度同时决定两件事：搜索范围外围的一小圈缓冲区，以及大约相当于半个像素的简化容差。

WITH tile AS (
    SELECT
        ST_TileEnvelope(z, x, y) AS bounds,
        (ST_XMax(bounds) - ST_XMin(bounds)) / 256.0 AS meters_per_pixel
),
candidates AS (
    SELECT
        f.id, f.geometry, tile.bounds,
        GREATEST(meters_per_pixel * 0.5, 0.1) AS tolerance
    FROM features f, tile
    WHERE ST_Intersects_Extent(
        f.geometry,
        ST_Buffer(tile.bounds, meters_per_pixel * 16)
    )
),
sampled AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM candidates
    USING SAMPLE reservoir(50000 ROWS)
),
encoded AS (
    SELECT
        id,
        ST_AsMVTGeom(
            ST_SimplifyPreserveTopology(geometry, tolerance),
            ST_Extent(bounds)
        ) AS geom
    FROM sampled
)
SELECT ST_AsMVT(encoded, 'features') AS tile
FROM encoded
WHERE geom IS NOT NULL;

ST_AsMVTGeom 把简化后的几何转换成瓦片坐标并做裁剪；ST_AsMVT 把这些几何及其属性打包成 Mapbox Vector Tile（MVT）。生产环境的实现还会处理无效几何、过滤掉非常小的线和多边形，并缓存已生成的瓦片。

地图请求的瓦片，由 Electron 桌面应用内部在本地运行的一个 HTTP 服务器提供。

Cosmograph：浏览器里探索百万级边的图谱

SQLRooms 也驱动着 Cosmograph 的分析工作区。Cosmograph 是一个基于浏览器的图谱探索工具，由 Nikita Rokotyan 和 Thor Whalen 开发，能可视化有数百万条边的图。Ilya 参与了把 SQLRooms 集成进这个应用的工作。

Cosmograph 测试过的数据集，从几万个点到几百万个点不等。DuckDB-Wasm 在后台 worker 里负责数据加载和 SQL 查询，帮助界面保持流畅。用户探索时，应用可以借它筛选和汇总数据；列式的查询结果也减少了为可视化准备数据所需的转换工作。

让 AI 智能体写 SQL

SQLRooms 也支持 AI 辅助分析。Ilya 说：“SQL 和 AI 智能体的组合其实相当强大。SQL 历史很长，网上有大量讲怎么用它的文档，所以大模型很擅长生成 SQL。”

用户可以用自然语言提问。助手生成 SQL 查询和图表规格，由应用在本地执行和渲染。源数据集可以留在用户电脑上，只把数据库结构和部分选定的查询结果发给 AI 服务商，帮助回答问题。

在下面这个 Spatial Desktop 示例里，助手生成 SQL，从可用数据源取数，并计算意大利各地适合种植葡萄的综合评分。生成的地图旁边附有 AI 生成的分区域分析。

SQLRooms 的下一步

Ilya 正在扩展 SQLRooms 的工作区模型，让用户可以把分析汇总到交互式文档里。这些文档把文字和图表、SQL 查询等区块组合在一起，用户可以在产出结论的分析旁边直接解释自己的发现。

Ilya 也在探索使用这些分析项目的其他方式。在阿姆斯特丹举办的 DuckCon #7 上，他演示了一个带笔记本式界面的 SQLRooms 命令行工具，它把数据和分析产物都保存在同一个 DuckDB 数据库文件里。目标是让用户可以在图形应用和命令行之间切换，继续同一个项目。这个 CLI 的设计仍在演变中。

延伸阅读

Ilya 在 DuckCon #7 上有一个五分钟的演讲，简要介绍了这个方向。

SQLRooms 是开源的，地址是 sqlrooms.org，可以从它的示例页入手。Flowmap City、Foursquare Spatial Desktop 和 Cosmograph 都可以免费试用。Ilya 关于 DuckDB 和 SQLRooms 的文章发布在他的个人网站上。

DuckDB 团队在文末感谢 Ilya 接受访谈，并邀请正在使用 DuckDB、愿意分享自己故事的读者发邮件给 geertjan@ducklabs.com。
